text: Shetland cast list in full as Gavin & Stacey star joins BBC drama for series 10 | Wales Online ‌ ‌ Skip to main content News Rugby Football What's On More Buy a Paper Funeral Notices Public Notices Jobs Directory Newsletter Signup Book an Ad Marketplace Buy a photo Wales Online Icon Lifestyle TV Shetland cast list in full as Gavin & Stacey star joins BBC drama for series 10 Shetland is back for series 10 and will see the much-loved team head to a small village in Scotland following the sinister murder of an elderly woman Lifestyle Megan Nisbet Content Editor 18:00, 05 Nov 2025 Updated 13:34, 10 Nov 2025 Shetland is returning for its tenth series, taking the beloved team to a quaint Scottish village following the chilling murder of an elderly woman. Fans of the enduring murder mystery drama will be delighted to see some familiar faces back on their screens. ‌ Alison O'Donnell and Ashley Jensen are reprising their roles as DI Alison 'Tosh' McIntosh and DI Ruth Calder, alongside Steven Robertson as Sandy and Lewis Howden as Sgt Billy McCabe. Samuel Anderson, known for his role in Gavin and Stacey as Fingers, joins the cast this year as Procurator Fiscal Matt Blake. ‌ Audiences may also recognise Samuel from his roles in Amandaland as Mal, Loaded as Leon, Trollied as Daniel, Doctor Who as Danny Pink, and Emmerdale as Ross Kirk between 2007 and 2009. ‌ In addition to the main cast, there's an impressive line-up of guest characters being introduced for series 10 as the team heads to the secluded hamlet of Lunniswick, where the body of retired social worker Eadie Tulloch has been exposed to the elements for several days. Guest stars include Clive Russell from Outlander and Game of Thrones, who previously appeared on Shetland in season two, Ellie Haddington from Motherland, Niall Macgregor from Line of Duty, Louise Brealey from Sherlock and Casualty, Greg McHugh from Fresh Meat, Frances Grey from Home Fires, and Stuart Townsend, known for The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen, reports the Daily Record . Shetland series 10 cast list Alison O'Donnell as DI Alison 'Tosh' Mcintosh ‌ View 5 Images Ashley Jensen and Alison O'Donnell in Shetland (Image: BBC/Silverprint Films/Jamie Simpson) Alison has been part of Shetland from the outset, initially appearing alongside Douglas Henshall before his departure from the role of DI Jimmy Perez in series seven. Discussing where Tosh finds herself at the beginning of series 10, Alison explained: "At the start of this new series, Tosh has really settled into her role as DI. Having reached a maturational threshold during season nine, realising that certain relationships were no longer serving her, she is knuckling down at work and focussing on the things in her life that truly matter." ‌ Alison's credits also include Holby City and the film Pet Sematary. Ashley Jensen as DI Ruth Calder Ashley succeeded Douglas in 2023, though prior to Shetland she gained recognition through Agatha Raisin, Afterlife, Catastrophe, Ugly Betty and Extras amongst numerous other productions. Regarding her character Calder's position in the new series, Ashley commented: "She's pretty settled into the police station and her life in Shetland. New photos from the set of HBO's upcoming Harry Potter TV series have given fans their first look at the show's cast in Hogwarts robes — which have been given a makeover from the previous movies. Harry Potter actor Dominic McLaughlin can be seen wearing a burgundy cloak, rather than the plain black coloring seen in the franchise's big-screen adaptation. Is this color a nod to the house colors of Gryffindor? It's hard to tell, though a glimpse of Lox Pratt, the young who plays Draco Malfoy, gives the impression he's wearing a slghtly different color indicative of Slytherin. FIRST LOOK at Harry, Draco Malfoy, Ron Weasley and Neville Longbottom in their Hogwarts robes in the HARRY POTTER TV series! pic.twitter.com/rfGHqQVBQh — Wizarding World Direct (@WW_Direct) November 11, 2025 These latest images, posted on social media by Wizarding World Direct , appear to show the filming of the first book's flying lesson scene, in which Draco steals Neville's Remembrall. The photos also provide our first look at Sherlock actress Louise Brealey in character as Madam Hooch, Hogwarts' broomstick instructor, who was previously potrayed by Zoë Wannamaker in the Harry Potter movies. Brealey is dressed in what looks to be a wizard-like version of a waterproof tracksuit — quite a different design to the dark robes Wannamaker wore. FIRST LOOK at Madam Hooch during flying lessons in the HARRY POTTER TV series 🧹 pic.twitter.com/nQygxYrSae — Wizarding World Direct (@WW_Direct) November 11, 2025 Last month, the Harry Potter TV production surprised fans by filming scenes mentioned but not directly included within the pages of the series' first book , featuring Dumbledore visiting Nicolas Flamel. But despite the huge interest in the show's production, fans have only caught glimpses of filming whenever production heads further afield from its base at Warner Bros.' Leavesdon Studios. Earlier peeks captured the moment Harry and the Dursleys visited London Zoo , as well as the scene where Hagrid leads Harry through London. Photos taken on that particular occaison prompted criticism from original Harry Potter movie director Chris Columbus , who asked "What's the point?" of a remake that looked too similar to the original. Defer too much from the books, however, and fans are likely to complain that HBO's new series is unauthentic. The Harry Potter TV series is expected to debut on HBO in early 2027 , with an eight-episode first season. Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. Filming on HBO’s Harry Potter series officially resumed this week — and fans just got their first look at one of the franchise’s most iconic early moments. At the historic Ashridge Estate in Hertfordshire, Dominic McLaughlin , who plays Harry Potter , was spotted shooting the first-year flying lesson sequence — the scene where Harry proves his natural talent on a broomstick for the very first time. Also spotted on the set were the likes of Louise Brealey as Madam Rolanda Hooch, Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, and Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy; the shoot marks the first on-set appearance of Malfoy, Neville and Madam Hooch, with Brealey stepping into the role originally played by Zoë Wanamaker in the film series. Although initial reports claimed it was a "Quidditch" scene, the presence of Hooch and the first-years in their uniforms gave away that this is in fact the original flying lesson from Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone — the moment where Harry takes off to chase Malfoy after he steals Neville’s Remembrall. It’s a pivotal scene that introduces Harry’s gift for flying, setting the stage for his future as Gryffindor’s Seeker. Of course, in classic Harry style, he does something he shouldn't and ends up getting rewarded for it. Classic Potter. Where Is 'Harry Potter' Being Filmed? And it's a familiar location too, for the franchise, as Ashridge Estate carries a special sense of déjà vu. The sprawling property was previously used during the production of Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire , serving as the forested backdrop for the Quidditch World Cup sequence. According to the National Trust, the estate’s Frithsden Beeches area once featured the gnarled tree from which Cedric Diggory ( Robert Pattinson ) jumps down in that film. Though the tree split in two in 2014, fans still visit the location to this day. Earlier this month, large-scale sets for the series were photographed in Hertfordshire, revealing what appeared to be a Hogwarts sports stand, Hagrid’s hut, and even the Weasley family’s Burrow. The series stars John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore and Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid, and will adapt J.K. Rowling ’s seven novels across multiple seasons, with plans to run through 2037 . The Harry Potter series is set to premiere on HBO in 2027. You can check out the first look at some of the characters embedded above. Dominic McLaughlin , the 11-year-old actor set to bring Harry Potter back to the screen in HBO’s 2027 remake, is also headlining the BBC’s new supernatural adventure series Gifted , which premieres November 24 on CBBC and iPlayer. And yes, the comparisons to Stranger Things are already flying. Gifted adapts Marilyn Kaye’s bestselling YA book series and follows a group of Scottish teens with extraordinary abilities — mind-reading, invisibility, telekinesis, and more. Filmed and set in Scotland, the story brings these powered kids together at a special school where they learn to control their gifts while fighting off a dangerous organization known as The Bodkin. Between the school setting, ensemble teen cast, and looming supernatural threat, the series is already being positioned as CBBC’s answer to Stranger Things — with a Wizarding World-style twist. The cast is made up of up-and-coming young Scottish actors, including McLaughlin , who steps into his first major onscreen role before taking on one of the biggest characters in literary and film history. And notably, McLaughlin is the exact same age Daniel Radcliffe was when he first suited up as Harry in 2001’s Sorcerer’s Stone . Produced by Black Camel Pictures (Glasgow) and Media Valley (Paris), Gifted will receive an international rollout in early 2026 — perfectly timed to introduce worldwide audiences to McLaughlin ahead of HBO’s Harry Potter , now in production and expected to debut in 2027. “Scottish kids clearly have talent and they want to act!” said executive producer Arabella Page Croft . “We are excited to produce this show for CBBC and bring these young talents and our beautiful capital city to a young audience globally.” NDR, who commissioned the series, praised Gifted for its mix of “ friendship, mystery and adventures ,” adding that it’s poised to be a major hit with younger viewers. Alongside McLaughlin, the young Hogwarts trio includes Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, with John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore , Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Esseidu as Severus Snape, and Nick Frost as Hagrid. Additional cast members include Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, Amos Kitson as Dudley Dursley, Louise Brealey as Madam Hooch, and Game of Thrones alum Anton Lesser as wandmaker Garrick Ollivander. Gifted premieres November 24 on CBBC and iPlayer, with international distribution rolling out in 2026. Credit: Hoda Davaine/Dave Benett/WireImage; Aidan Monaghan/HBO The magic of Harry Potter is continuing into a TV series, and Rupert Grint has given his full support to the new young actor taking over his previous role as Ron Weasley. Grint, 37, revealed that he reached out to Alastair Stout, who will play Ron in HBO's upcoming TV adaptation of J.K. Rowling's young adult series. "I wrote him a letter, before they started [filming]," Grint told BBC News . "Passing the baton, as it were." While Grint — who starred in all eight Harry Potter movies as part of the original trio of wizards — "can't remember exactly" what he wrote in his letter to Stout, it was "something to that effect" of feeling "really happy for him," and that the TV series is "really exciting." "I’m really intrigued [about] what it’s going to be like," Grint said. "It’s quite strange, having it, the cycle, happen again. I had so much fun stepping into this world, and I hope he has the same experience." Rupert Grint in 'Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone'. Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection Stout, along with Dominic McLaughlin (who will play Harry) and Arabella Stanton (who will play Hermione Granger), was cast in the series in May. When Grint heard the casting news, it "took me straight back [to] when we first got the parts." Grint added, "It was a big thing. I still remember every second of it. It's a big moment, and I just want him to enjoy it." As for Stout's red hair and freckles, which are required to play a Weasley, Grint joked, "There's a bit of family resemblance." Last week, Daniel Radcliffe also revealed that he had reached out to the young actor taking over his titular role via a letter. "I know a few people that are working on the production, so I wrote to Dominic and I sent him a letter, and he sent me a very sweet note back," Radcliffe said during an appearance on Good Morning America , but added, "I do not want to be a specter in the lives of these children at all." In his letter, Radcliffe said that he expressed, "I hope you have the best time, and an even better time than I did. I had a great time, but I hope you have an even better one." Rowling and is open to having a conversation HBO's upcoming Harry Potter series (currently in production) is from showrunner Francesca Gardiner and director Mark Mylod , both also executive producers, and will debut in 2027 on HBO and HBO Max. It has been billed as a faithful adaptation, expanding each of Rowling's seven books into individual seasons. "I think it’s great that it’s a whole new thing," Grint said. "It’s going to be its own thing, and I think that will be fun." Other cast members include: John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape, Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid, Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy, Johnny Flynn as Lucius Malfoy, Janet McTeer as Minvera McGonagall, Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom, Amos Kitson as Dudley Dursley, Louise Brealey has Madame Hooch, and Anton Lesser as Ollivander. Franchise alum Warwick Davis , who played Professor Filius Flitwick across all eight Harry Potter films, is reprising his role for the HBO series. Rowling has become a controversial figure in recent years due to her vocal transphobic views shared on social media. She is also attached to the project as an executive producer, and revealed that she "worked closely" with the writers' room . However, HBO chairman and CEO Casey Bloys assured that the series would not be "secretly infused" with anti-trans rhetoric and that Rowling was ultimately "entitled" to her own views. "I've said this before, but the decision to be in business with J.K. Rowling is not new for us," Bloys said earlier this year. "We've been in business for 25 years. Photograph: Sarah Meyssonnier/Reuters Audiobooks Ncuti Gatwa leads star winners at first Speakies awards for audio storytelling The actor won best performance for BBC drama Gatsby in Harlem at the inaugural British Audio awards, while Nicola Coughlan’s narration of Juno Dawson’s Queen B clinched best sci-fi audiobook Emma Loffhagen Mon 24 Nov 2025 16.00 EST Last modified on Mon 24 Nov 2025 16.02 EST Share Audiobooks narrated by Ncuti Gatwa, Nicola Coughlan and David Tennant were among those recognised at the inaugural British Audio awards, the “Speakies”. Gatwa’s performance in the lead role of Gatsby in Harlem helped it emerge as one of Monday evening’s biggest winners: it took three major prizes including audio of the year. The reimagining of Fitzgerald’s The Great Gatsby also won best audio drama adaptation, while Gatwa took home the best performance award for what organisers described as his “remarkable poise and flair” in capturing Gatsby’s character. The Speakies are the UK’s first set of prizes dedicated to audiobooks and audio drama. The inaugural ceremony, held at the Royal Opera House and hosted by actor and comedian Sally Phillips, celebrated what the prize called the full “ecosystem” of audio storytelling – from writers and actors to sound designers and publishers – at a moment when listening figures and investment across the sector continue to climb. Best audiobook: science fiction and fantasy went to Juno Dawson’s Queen B, a witchcraft novel about Anne Boleyn, narrated by Nicola Coughlan. The Bridgerton star “brings wit and vivacity to her telling and successfully whisks readers away from the 21st century to the heart of King Henry VIII’s court,” said category judging chair Katie Fraser. View image in fullscreen Clever family … JD Kirk’s Him, co-narrated by David Tennant, left, won best crime audiobook at the Speakies; while Georgia Tennant, right, accepted the best romance audiobook award for her narration of Jilly Cooper’s Rivals. Photograph: Dave Benett/Alan Chapman/Getty Images JD Kirk’s Him, narrated by David Tennant and Louise Brealey, won best audiobook: crime and thriller. The win came on the same night Tennant’s wife, Georgia Tennant, accepted the best romance audiobook award on behalf of the team behind Rivals, Jilly Cooper’s 1988 novel, newly adapted for audio to coincide with its recent Disney+ screen adaptation. Tribute was paid to Cooper, who died last month . In nonfiction, the best audiobook: memoir prize went to Careless People by Sarah Wynn-Williams , her whistleblowing account of speaking out about Meta. Self-narrated, the audiobook was described as a “powerful reclamation of speech and agency”. Why Are You Here, Mrs Hamilton?, a memoir by Post Office scandal victim Jo Hamilton narrated by Monica Dolan – who portrayed her in ITV’s television drama Mr Bates vs the Post Office – took home best nonfiction audiobook. Meanwhile, Mark Gatiss won best performance as a narrator for his reading of Ian Fleming’s From Russia With Love, edging out Stephen Fry among others. Independent publishers made a strong showing at the Speakies. Galley Beggar Press and Spiracle Audio beat major houses to win best fiction audiobook with All My Precious Madness by Mark Bowles, narrated by Paul Hilton. The audiobook was praised for its “ambitious concept” and inventive use of multiple voices, and described as an example of audio evolving as a form in its own right. According to the Publishers Association, audiobook sales in the UK rose by 31% in 2024 , reaching a record £268m. Last week, a study from the National Literacy Trust found that while only 32% of young people said that they read for enjoyment, 42% enjoyed listening to audiobooks. Philip Jones, editor of the Bookseller – which co-runs the new awards with the Stage – said the awards reflected a “moment” for UK audio. “I am delighted with our winners for this first year,” he said. “As listener interest grows, investment across platforms and talent increases, and excellence across disciplines rises to the occasion. Bringing this all together under one awards banner for the first time, with all of the talent recognised, truly has been a joy to behold.” This year’s judges included Gavin & Stacey star Laura Aikman, broadcaster and author Michelle Elman, author Abir Mukherjee, Doctor Who star Pearl Mackie, YouTuber Hannah Witton and Guardian audiobook critic Fiona Sturges. text: Who killed Eadie Tulloch in Shetland series 10? 5 theories explained - The Mirror ‌ ‌ Skip to main content News Celebs Football Lifestyle More InYourArea Funeral Notices Shop Competitions Dating Offers Newsletter Signup Follow us on social Daily Mirror Icon TV TV News Documentaries Who killed Eadie Tulloch in Shetland series 10? 5 theories explained Shetland series 10 has captivated viewers with Eadie Tulloch's murder mystery. As the BBC thriller unfolds, fans are theorising about who killed Eadie, and here are the top 5 suspects TV Megan Nisbet Content Editor 12:40, 25 Nov 2025 View 7 Images Ashley Jenson as DI Ruth Calder on Shetland (Image: BBC/Silverprint Films/Jamie Simpson) Shetland has returned for its tenth series, with Alison O'Donnell and Ashley Jensen reprising their roles as DI Alison 'Tosh' McIntosh and DI Ruth Calder, as they probe the mysterious killing of Eadie Tulloch. ‌ The former social worker was discovered deceased outside her home in the remote hamlet of Lunniswick, having been exposed to the harsh weather for several days before her neighbour Colin Waite, portrayed by Greg McHugh, found her whilst delivering a food parcel. ‌ Eadie's unexpected death has sent shockwaves through the tight-knit community, with every resident falling under suspicion. The investigation has become increasingly puzzling as there were no indications of any disturbance inside Eadie's property, leading Calder to deduce that she was probably pulled from her bed whilst wearing her nightdress, with no evidence of resistance. ‌ View 7 Images Ashley Jenson as DI Ruth Calder on Shetland (Image: BBC/Silverprint Films/Jamie Simpson) In the opening episode, Calder questioned Tosh: "Why the effort of dragging her outside, tying her up, and posing her body?" With the perpetrator still unidentified, Calder and Tosh have been examining Eadie's background, uncovering a bank account containing £400,000 in cash, which contradicts the modest lifestyle Eadie appeared to lead. Investigations have also discovered she was wed to Police Sergeant Robert Tulloch and had a son, Ed Tulloch, portrayed by Stuart Townsend, with whom she'd lost contact before her death. Initial suspicion fell on David Powell, a neighbour with a chequered history who'd visited Eadie's property prior to the killing, though it emerged David had simply befriended Eadie and was helping renovate her bathroom at the time of her death. So who's now under the spotlight? ‌ From Eadie's neighbour Lana Mair, portrayed by Motherland's Ellie Haddington, to her own son Ed, here are the key theories surrounding the series 10 murder. Ed Tulloch View 7 Images Stuart Townsend as Ed Tulloch and Ashley Jensen's DI Ruth Calder (Image: BBC/Silverprint Films/Jamie Simpson) Eadie's son Ed, portrayed by Stuart Townsend, must surely be considered a suspect, particularly given their estrangement. Despite managing a pub nearby, they "argued about everything" and barely spoke, reports the Daily Record . ‌ Ed's fractured relationship with his mother has led him to bond with Calder, who also has a difficult relationship with her own father. However, their friendship could complicate matters, particularly if Ed proves to be the perpetrator. For the moment, though, Ed has insisted he knew nothing about the funds in his mum's bank account. Lana Mair View 7 Images Clive Russell as Arthur Mair and Ellie Haddington as Lana Mair (Image: BBC/Silverprint Films/Jamie Simpson) ‌ Lana, portrayed by Motherland's Ellie Haddington, is Eadie's neighbour who attracted attention after the rather significant act of torching Eadie's entire property following her murder. Although it's far more probable that Lana, who suffers from dementia, possesses vital information about the investigation and was attempting to conceal it rather than being the killer herself. Colin Waite View 7 Images Colin Waite on Shetland (Image: BBC/Silverprint Films/Jamie Simpson) Colin, portrayed by Fresh Meat's Greg Mchugh, was first to discover Eadie after dropping off a food parcel at her residence, and was also the final person to see her following an interview for his island documentary project. Colin was swift to accuse David Powell, singling out the young man because of his criminal history, which could be interpreted as suspicious conduct. ‌ Stevie Shannon View 7 Images Stevie Shannon is a suspect on Shetland The opening episode disclosed that newcomer Chris had noticed someone at Eadie's property on the night of her death. Episode three unveiled that Stevie Shannon, portrayed by Chloe-Ann Tylor, was the mysterious individual, a detail she concealed from authorities fearing she might fall under suspicion. She confided in her sister: "I don't know why I went to see her last Saturday. I didn't do anything, I just stood outside her house watching her through the window." ‌ Isobel Jameson View 7 Images Isobel Jameson on Shetland (Image: BBC) Somewhat unexpected but it's often those you least suspect. Isobel, portrayed by Sherlock star Louise Brealey, seems to be a caring neighbour and devoted mum looking after her expectant teenage daughter but everything isn't as it appears. There's tension brewing between Isobel and Margaret, the mother of her daughter's baby daddy, despite their past close friendship. The plot thickens as we're left guessing how this ties in with Eadie, but one thing's for sure - there are enough family secrets to make anyone's eyebrows shoot up. text: Shetland season 10 cast: Every character, new and returning Search Entertainment Beauty Love and Sex Fashion News and Politics Body Quizzes Lifestyle Work Horoscopes Videos Newsletter Subscribe Win Shop Events Follow Cookies Policy Other Editions Privacy Notice Terms Of Use Skip to Content Celebs Love Beauty Fashion Shopping Body Subscribe Newsletter 8 matte foundations How to wear brown Best protective hairstyles Black Friday Deals London's best bars Entertainment TV Shetland season 10 cast: Every character, new and returning Shetland season 10 cast: Every character, new and returning Meet the cast members joining Ashley and Alison By Megan Wallace Updated: 12 November 2025 Shetland is officially back for its tenth season. The TV show, which is beloved by fans of police dramas like Trigger Point and Karen Pirie , has been running since all the way back in 2013. And we're seriously obsessed with the new season. This time around sees Calder and Tosh begin the investigation into the death of retired social worker Eadie Tulloch in the small hamlet of Lunniswick, with nearly every person in the village being treated as a suspect and as the pair get deeper into the crime, they realise this small town is holding a lot of secrets. And with a new crime means new cast, so here's everything to know about the new cast for Shetland season 10 and of course all the details on the returning cast. Jump to: Shetland season 10 returning cast Shetland season 10 new cast Shetland season 10 returning cast The new series of Shetland will see the return of series regulars, including: Ashley Jensen as DI Ruth Calder Photographer: // BBC Who is DI Ruth Calder? DI Ruth Calder is one of the main characters of Shetland . She's a Shetland native but has returned to the area after some years working for the Metropolitan Police in London for twenty years. She replaced lead investigator Jimmy Perez from season 8, onwards. What else has Ashley Jensen been in? You may well recognise Ashley Jensen as Christina in Ugly Betty , Maggie in Extras and Agatha in Agatha Raisin . Alison O’Donnell as DI Alison ‘Tosh’ MacIntosh PHOTOGRAPHER:Jamie Simpson // BBC Who is DI Alison ‘Tosh’ MacIntosh? DI Alison ‘Tosh’ MacIntosh was formerly a Detective Sergeant on the team but was promoted in later seasons of the show. She's been working on the Lerwick Police Station team since the beginning of the show, and audiences have seen her grow in maturity and confidence. This season, she goes on a journey as she grapples with a personal conflict. What else has Alison O’Donnell been in? Alison O'Donnell is best known for her role in Shetland , but is also a popular theatre actress in Scotland. Steven Robertson as DC Sandy Wilson Photographer: // BBC Who is DC Sandy Wilson ? DC Sandy Wilson is a hard-working and dedicated Detective Constable whose knowledge of the local island and community has proven indispensable when solving crimes. What else has Steven Robertson been in? He has played Mark in The Bay , Tom in Vera , Tom in New Tricks , Robert in Luther , Robert in Harlots and Dominic in Being Human . Lewis Howden as Sgt Billy McCabe Photographer: // BBC Who is Sgt Billy McCabe? Sgt Billy McCabe is in charge of the desk at the local station, and is a well-liked member of the team among the island community. What else has Lewis Howden been in? Lewis Howden has appeared in Taggart and Rebus as well as the film Meet You in Scotland . Anne Kidd as Cora McLean Photographer: // BBC Who is Cora McLean ? Cora McLean is a forensic pathologist who utilises her medical expertise to help the Shetland police on crime scenes. What else has Anne Kidd been in? Anne Kid has appeared in major shows such as Doctors , Outlander and Vigil . Angus Miller as Donnie BBC Who is Donnie? Donnie is Tosh's partner and the father of her child. What else has Angus Miller been in? Angus Miller is a prolific theatre actor in Scotland. Conor McCarry as PC Alex Grant BBC Who is PC Alex Grant? PC Alex Grant is one of the younger team members on the Lerwick Police Station team. What else has Conor McCarry been in? Conor McMarry is known for playing the role of Young Jamie in Outlander . Eubha Akilade as PC Lorna Burns Photographer: // BBC Who is PC Lorna Burns? Another younger officer on the Lerwick Police Station team, PC Lorna Burns is ambitious and keen to prove herself to her colleagues. What else has Eubha Akilade been in? Eubha Akilade co-wrote and directed on the BBC monologue series “The Wedding”. Steven Miller as Rev Alan Calder BBC Who is Rev Alan Calder? Rev Alan is DI Ruth's estranged brother. What else has Steven Miller been in? You'll most likely recognise Steven from his role in Dept Q . He's also been in Our Girl, Payback, The Walk-In and Traces . Shetland season 10 new cast Samuel Anderson as Procurator Fiscal Matt Blake PHOTOGRAPHER:Jamie Simpson // BBC Who is Procurator Fiscal Matt Blake? Procurator Fiscal Matt Blake is a Scottish public prosecutor and will decide whether crimes should be prosecuted in the public interest. What else has Samuel Anderson been in? Samuel Anderson has appeared most recently as Mal in the Motherland spin off Amandaland and also appeared as Fingers on Gavin and Stacey . Clive Russell as Arthur Mair PHOTOGRAPHER:Jamie Simpson // BBC Who is Arthur Mair? Born and bred in Shetland, Arthur Mair spent most of his working life on the oil rigs. Kind, caring and uncomplaining, Arthur is very much a ‘doer’ rather than a ‘talker’. Family is important to Arthur, and he has a particularly close relationship with his granddaughter Jess, as well as being the sole carer of his wife Lana, who has vascular dementia. What else has Clive Russell been in? Clive Russell is best known for playing Stribog in The Witcher , Lord Lovat in Outlander and Brynden Tully in Game of Thrones . Ellie Haddington as Lana Mair PHOTOGRAPHER:Jamie Simpson // BBC Who is Lana Mair? Originally from Aberdeen, Lana moved to Shetland when she met her husband, Arthur, where she also became close friends with Eadie Tulloch. Before the tragic loss of her son Ally over two decades ago, Lana was a positive and warm person. However, Ally’s death took its toll on Lana as she was overwhelmed with grief. In the past few years, Lana has developed dementia and requires support from her family. What else has Ellie Haddington been in? Ellie Haddington played Josie Clarke in Coronation Street in 1995 to 1996. From 2016 to 2022, she played Julia's mother on Motherland. Niall Macgregor as Tom Jameson Photographer: // BBC Who is Tom Jameson? Stoic, tacit and unemotional, Tom believes in actions rather than words. Due to a recent heart condition, he’s been unable to work for 18 months, and has been forced to move in with his in-laws, Arthur and Lana Mair, along with his wife Isobel and pregnant teenage daughter Jess. He’s a conflicted and complex character who’s struggling to adapt to his new reality. As a person who always prided himself on providing for his family, Tom’s unsure of who he is anymore. What else has Niall Macgregor been in? Niall Macgregor appeared as Rich in Line of Duty. Louise Brealey as Isobel Jameson Photographer: // BBC Who is Isobel Jameson? Born and bred in quiet hamlet of Lunniswick, Isobel is cheery and hard-working, always putting others before herself - especially her family. Isobel believes that in spite of all the struggles her family is going through – husband Tom’s illness, her mother’s dementia, daughter Jess’s unplanned pregnancy – it’ll all come good once her first grandchild arrives. Isobel is hopeful that a new life will bring much-needed joy and focus to the family. However, her optimism will be tested to the limits when tragedy casts a shadow over Lunniswick. What else has Louise Brealey been in? Deb in Such Brave Girls , Molly in Sherlock , Cass in Back , Jude in Clique and Gillian in A Discovery of Witches . Lila Rose as Jess Jameson Who is Jess Jameson? The only child of Tom and Isobel Jameson, teenager Jess is a perfect mix of both her parents, possessing her father’s temper and her mum’s optimism. Jess is an excellent student and was all set for university until she fell pregnant. Partly due to pressure from her mother, Jess decided to keep the baby. However, with the birth date looming, Jess feels increasingly exiled and is starting to have second thoughts about motherhood. What else has Lila Rose been in? Lila Rose played Kitty in season two of Traces . Greg McHugh as Colin Waite Photographer: // BBC Who is Colin Waite? A well-known local figure, Colin Waite knows everyone in Lunniswick - and their business. That’s why, for some, he’s seen as nosey and a bit judgemental. In recent months, Colin has thrown himself into pulling together the history of the village. Through his research chats, Colin grew close to murder victim Eadie, looking out for her when others turned a blind eye. So, for all his faults, Colin can be kind and thoughtful. That doesn’t change the fact he’s a little eccentric and peculiar. What else has Greg McHugh been in? Greg McHugh is best known as the star and creator of Gary: Tank Commander and Howard on Fresh Meat . Frances Grey as Gina Powell Photographer: // BBC Who is Gina Powell? Life hasn’t always been easy on Gina Powell, especially not of late. Gina can be guarded and untrusting, but she wasn’t always this way – her life took a turn for the worst after her husband was sent to prison for armed robbery and then abandoned her on his release, leaving Gina to raise their son, David, alone. Feeling judged by the locals, Gina distanced herself from her neighbours and has a reputation for being prickly and unapproachable. David is the sole focus in Gina’s life and his recent prison stint has stirred up painful memories from the past, making her more anxious and fearful than ever. What else has Frances Grey been in? Frances Grey appeared as Olivia on Vera . Stephen McMillan as David Powell Who is David Powell? Painfully shy, lacking in confidence and easily influenced, David spent the last eighteen months in prison serving time for housebreaking. Since his release, David has been living back with his mum, Gina, in Lunniswick and is trying to recover from his ordeal. Despite David’s criminality, he is not a bad person. He has made poor choices and this, combined with some bad luck, has sent him down the wrong path. Lonely and anxious, David struck up an odd friendship with Eadie but her murder will bring heartbreak and unwanted attention to him. All David wants is to rebuild his life but that’s easier said than done. What else has Stephen McMillan been in? Stephen McMillan is best known as Jamie on Boiling Point and also featured in Toxic Town. Saskia Ashdown as Hayley Burnett BBC Who is Hayley Burnett? Hayley and her family have travelled to Lunniswick for a family holiday, however, they soon find themselves caught up in the drama of Eadie's murder. What else has Saskia Ashdown been in? Saskia has previously appeared in series such as Karen Pirie, The Rig and Annika. Gabriel Akuwudike as Chris Burnett BBC Who is Chris Burnett? Chris is Hayley's husband and manages to insert himself into the investigation after revealing he saw a young man near Eadie's house to the police. What else has Gabriel Akuwudike been in? You'll most likely recognise Gabriel from his role as Hagen in L ord of the Rings: The Rings of Power , as well as starring in the series Hanna and Screw . Stuart Townsend as Edward ‘Ed’ Tulloch Photographer: // BBC Who is Ed Tulloch? Handsome and charming, Ed Tulloch has a certain undeniable allure about him. In his younger years, Ed was a successful poet and his work is well-known across the Shetland Isles. These days, he’s a businessman in the drinks trade but poetry is in his DNA. Ed’s grief about his mother’s murder is tinged with regret as he had become estranged from Eadie in recent years. For all his charm and easy humour, there’s a sadness to Ed and it’s clear there’s something deeper underneath. What else has Stuart Townsend been in? Stuart Townsend is known for roles in Into the Deep and Two Minutes to Midnight. Chloe-Ann Tylor as Stevie Shannon BBC Who is Stevie Shannon? Stevie is a new character for the series but so far not much has been revealed about her role. What else has Chloe-Ann Tylor been in? Chloe-Ann is known for her theatre work. Joanne Thomson as Amy Shannon BBC Who is Amy Shannon? Amy is a new character for the series and so far not much is known about her role. What else has Joanne Thomson been in? Joanne is best known for her role of Amy in Outlander. She's also been in Betrayal , In Plain Sight and The Victim . Adam Rhazali as Will Lowden Who is Will Lowden? Will is a new character for the series but not much is known about his role so far. What else has Adam Rhazali been in? Shetland is Adam's first major role. Leigh Biagi as Morag McCabe BBC Who is Morag McCabe?: After 10 seasons we will finally get to meet Billy's wife, who knew the victim Eadie. What else has Leigh Biagi been in?: Most recently you will recognise Leigh from her role as Mother Superior in the new Frankenstein movie. She's also known for The Lost King and Neds . Jump to: Shetland season 10 returning cast Shetland season 10 new cast Shetland season 10 returning cast The new series of Shetland will see the return of series regulars, including: Ashley Jensen as DI Ruth Calder Photographer: // BBC Who is DI Ruth Calder? DI Ruth Calder is one of the main characters of Shetland. She's a Shetland native but has returned to the area after some years working for the Metropolitan Police in London for twenty years. She replaced lead investigator Jimmy Perez from season 8, onwards. What else has Ashley Jensen been in? You may well recognise Ashley Jensen as Christina in Ugly Betty , Maggie in Extras and Agatha in Agatha Raisin. Alison O’Donnell as DI Alison ‘Tosh’ MacIntosh PHOTOGRAPHER:Jamie Simpson // BBC Who is DI Alison ‘Tosh’ MacIntosh? DI Alison ‘Tosh’ MacIntosh was formerly a Detective Sergeant on the team but was promoted in later seasons of the show. She's been working on the Lerwick Police Station team since the beginning of the show, and audiences have seen her grow in maturity and confidence. This season, she goes on a journey as she grapples with a personal conflict. What else has Alison O’Donnell been in? Alison O'Donnell is best known for her role in Shetland , but is also a popular theatre actress in Scotland. Steven Robertson as DC Sandy Wilson Photographer: // BBC Who is DC Sandy Wilson ? DC Sandy Wilson is a hard-working and dedicated Detective Constable whose knowledge of the local island and community has proven indispensable when solving crimes. What else has Steven Robertson been in? He has played Mark in The Bay , Tom in Vera , Tom in New Tricks , Robert in Luther , Robert in Harlots and Dominic in Being Human. Lewis Howden as Sgt Billy McCabe Photographer: // BBC Who is Sgt Billy McCabe? Sgt Billy McCabe is in charge of the desk at the local station, and is a well-liked member of the team among the island community. What else has Lewis Howden been in? Lewis Howden has appeared in Taggart and Rebus as well as the film Meet You in Scotland. Anne Kidd as Cora McLean Photographer: // BBC Who is Cora McLean ? Cora McLean is a forensic pathologist who utilises her medical expertise to help the Shetland police on crime scenes. What else has Anne Kidd been in? Anne Kid has appeared in major shows such as Doctors , Outlander and Vigil. Angus Miller as Donnie BBC Who is Donnie? Donnie is Tosh's partner and the father of her child. What else has Angus Miller been in? Angus Miller is a prolific theatre actor in Scotland. Conor McCarry as PC Alex Grant BBC Who is PC Alex Grant? PC Alex Grant is one of the younger team members on the Lerwick Police Station team. What else has Conor McCarry been in? Conor McMarry is known for playing the role of Young Jamie in Outlander. Eubha Akilade as PC Lorna Burns Photographer: // BBC Who is PC Lorna Burns? Another younger officer on the Lerwick Police Station team, PC Lorna Burns is ambitious and keen to prove herself to her colleagues. What else has Eubha Akilade been in? Eubha Akilade co-wrote and directed on the BBC monologue series “The Wedding”. Steven Miller as Rev Alan Calder BBC Who is Rev Alan Calder? Rev Alan is DI Ruth's estranged brother. What else has Steven Miller been in? You'll most likely recognise Steven from his role in Dept Q. He's also been in Our Girl, Payback, The Walk-In and Traces. Shetland season 10 new cast Samuel Anderson as Procurator Fiscal Matt Blake PHOTOGRAPHER:Jamie Simpson // BBC Who is Procurator Fiscal Matt Blake? Procurator Fiscal Matt Blake is a Scottish public prosecutor and will decide whether crimes should be prosecuted in the public interest. What else has Samuel Anderson been in? Samuel Anderson has appeared most recently as Mal in the Motherland spin off Amandaland and also appeared as Fingers on Gavin and Stacey. Clive Russell as Arthur Mair PHOTOGRAPHER:Jamie Simpson // BBC Who is Arthur Mair? Born and bred in Shetland, Arthur Mair spent most of his working life on the oil rigs. Kind, caring and uncomplaining, Arthur is very much a ‘doer’ rather than a ‘talker’. Family is important to Arthur, and he has a particularly close relationship with his granddaughter Jess, as well as being the sole carer of his wife Lana, who has vascular dementia. What else has Clive Russell been in? Clive Russell is best known for playing Stribog in The Witcher , Lord Lovat in Outlander and Brynden Tully in Game of Thrones. Ellie Haddington as Lana Mair PHOTOGRAPHER:Jamie Simpson // BBC Who is Lana Mair? Originally from Aberdeen, Lana moved to Shetland when she met her husband, Arthur, where she also became close friends with Eadie Tulloch. Before the tragic loss of her son Ally over two decades ago, Lana was a positive and warm person. However, Ally’s death took its toll on Lana as she was overwhelmed with grief. In the past few years, Lana has developed dementia and requires support from her family. What else has Ellie Haddington been in? Ellie Haddington played Josie Clarke in Coronation Street in 1995 to 1996. From 2016 to 2022, she played Julia's mother on Motherland. Niall Macgregor as Tom Jameson Photographer: // BBC Who is Tom Jameson? Stoic, tacit and unemotional, Tom believes in actions rather than words. Due to a recent heart condition, he’s been unable to work for 18 months, and has been forced to move in with his in-laws, Arthur and Lana Mair, along with his wife Isobel and pregnant teenage daughter Jess. He’s a conflicted and complex character who’s struggling to adapt to his new reality. As a person who always prided himself on providing for his family, Tom’s unsure of who he is anymore. What else has Niall Macgregor been in? Niall Macgregor appeared as Rich in Line of Duty. Louise Brealey as Isobel Jameson Photographer: // BBC Who is Isobel Jameson? Born and bred in quiet hamlet of Lunniswick, Isobel is cheery and hard-working, always putting others before herself - especially her family. Isobel believes that in spite of all the struggles her family is going through – husband Tom’s illness, her mother’s dementia, daughter Jess’s unplanned pregnancy – it’ll all come good once her first grandchild arrives. Isobel is hopeful that a new life will bring much-needed joy and focus to the family. However, her optimism will be tested to the limits when tragedy casts a shadow over Lunniswick. What else has Louise Brealey been in? Deb in Such Brave Girls , Molly in Sherlock , Cass in Back , Jude in Clique and Gillian in A Discovery of Witches. Lila Rose as Jess Jameson Who is Jess Jameson? The only child of Tom and Isobel Jameson, teenager Jess is a perfect mix of both her parents, possessing her father’s temper and her mum’s optimism. Jess is an excellent student and was all set for university until she fell pregnant. Partly due to pressure from her mother, Jess decided to keep the baby. However, with the birth date looming, Jess feels increasingly exiled and is starting to have second thoughts about motherhood. What else has Lila Rose been in? Lila Rose played Kitty in season two of Traces. Greg McHugh as Colin Waite Photographer: // BBC Who is Colin Waite? A well-known local figure, Colin Waite knows everyone in Lunniswick - and their business. That’s why, for some, he’s seen as nosey and a bit judgemental. In recent months, Colin has thrown himself into pulling together the history of the village. Through his research chats, Colin grew close to murder victim Eadie, looking out for her when others turned a blind eye. So, for all his faults, Colin can be kind and thoughtful. That doesn’t change the fact he’s a little eccentric and peculiar. What else has Greg McHugh been in? Greg McHugh is best known as the star and creator of Gary: Tank Commander and Howard on Fresh Meat. Frances Grey as Gina Powell Photographer: // BBC Who is Gina Powell? Life hasn’t always been easy on Gina Powell, especially not of late. Gina can be guarded and untrusting, but she wasn’t always this way – her life took a turn for the worst after her husband was sent to prison for armed robbery and then abandoned her on his release, leaving Gina to raise their son, David, alone. Feeling judged by the locals, Gina distanced herself from her neighbours and has a reputation for being prickly and unapproachable. David is the sole focus in Gina’s life and his recent prison stint has stirred up painful memories from the past, making her more anxious and fearful than ever. What else has Frances Grey been in? Frances Grey appeared as Olivia on Vera. Stephen McMillan as David Powell Who is David Powell? Painfully shy, lacking in confidence and easily influenced, David spent the last eighteen months in prison serving time for housebreaking. Since his release, David has been living back with his mum, Gina, in Lunniswick and is trying to recover from his ordeal. Despite David’s criminality, he is not a bad person. He has made poor choices and this, combined with some bad luck, has sent him down the wrong path. Lonely and anxious, David struck up an odd friendship with Eadie but her murder will bring heartbreak and unwanted attention to him. All David wants is to rebuild his life but that’s easier said than done. What else has Stephen McMillan been in? Stephen McMillan is best known as Jamie on Boiling Point and also featured in Toxic Town. Saskia Ashdown as Hayley Burnett BBC Who is Hayley Burnett? Hayley and her family have travelled to Lunniswick for a family holiday, however, they soon find themselves caught up in the drama of Eadie's murder. What else has Saskia Ashdown been in? Saskia has previously appeared in series such as Karen Pirie, The Rig and Annika. Gabriel Akuwudike as Chris Burnett BBC Who is Chris Burnett? Chris is Hayley's husband and manages to insert himself into the investigation after revealing he saw a young man near Eadie's house to the police. What else has Gabriel Akuwudike been in? You'll most likely recognise Gabriel from his role as Hagen in L ord of the Rings: The Rings of Power , as well as starring in the series Hanna and Screw. Stuart Townsend as Edward ‘Ed’ Tulloch Photographer: // BBC Who is Ed Tulloch? Handsome and charming, Ed Tulloch has a certain undeniable allure about him. In his younger years, Ed was a successful poet and his work is well-known across the Shetland Isles. These days, he’s a businessman in the drinks trade but poetry is in his DNA. Ed’s grief about his mother’s murder is tinged with regret as he had become estranged from Eadie in recent years. For all his charm and easy humour, there’s a sadness to Ed and it’s clear there’s something deeper underneath. What else has Stuart Townsend been in? Stuart Townsend is known for roles in Into the Deep and Two Minutes to Midnight. Chloe-Ann Tylor as Stevie Shannon BBC Who is Stevie Shannon? Stevie is a new character for the series but so far not much has been revealed about her role. What else has Chloe-Ann Tylor been in? Chloe-Ann is known for her theatre work. Joanne Thomson as Amy Shannon BBC Who is Amy Shannon? Amy is a new character for the series and so far not much is known about her role. What else has Joanne Thomson been in? Joanne is best known for her role of Amy in Outlander. She's also been in Betrayal , In Plain Sight and The Victim. Adam Rhazali as Will Lowden Who is Will Lowden? Will is a new character for the series but not much is known about his role so far. What else has Adam Rhazali been in? Shetland is Adam's first major role. Leigh Biagi as Morag McCabe BBC Who is Morag McCabe?: After 10 seasons we will finally get to meet Billy's wife, who knew the victim Eadie. What else has Leigh Biagi been in?: Most recently you will recognise Leigh from her role as Mother Superior in the new Frankenstein movie. She's also known for The Lost King and Neds. Email tips@dailymail.co.uk By EMMA GUINNESS and ALEX DOYLE - SENIOR SHOWBUSINESS REPORTER Published: 11:17 EST, 17 November 2025 | Updated: 11:45 EST, 17 November 2025 e-mail 1 View comments The star of HBO 's hotly-anticipated Harry Potter TV show Dominic McLaughlin is set to take centre stage this month in a new Stranger Things-inspired TV show. Gifted, which will air on CBBC from November 24, is centred around a group of teens who all have special gifts - from mind-reading to invisibility to telekinesis. Set and filmed in Scotland, the action-adventure drama follows the gifted teenagers as they bring their powers together to save themselves and their loved ones from a powerful organisation - the Bodkin. The show has echoes of not only Stranger Things , but Harry Potter too and the teens all attend a special school in a bid to hone and better control their unique gifts. Gifted is based on the novel series of the same name by Marilyn Kaye and will introduce TV fans to a number of young, up-and-coming Scottish actors. This, of course, includes Dominic McLaughlin, 11, who has also been cast as Harry Potter in the first television of JK Rowling 's hit novels. The show is a co-production between the Glasgow-based production company Black Camel Pictures and Media Valley, who are based in Paris. It is scheduled for international distribution in early 2026, giving young people a chance to get to know Dominic McLaughlin ahead of his starring role in the Harry Potter show, which is expected to be released in 2027. Arabella Page Croft, Executive Producer at Black Camel Pictures, said: 'Scottish kids clearly have talent and they want to act! 'We are excited to produce this show for CBBC and bring these young talents and our beautiful capital city to a young audience globally.' NDR, who commissioned Gifted, praised the series for being a story with many appealing elements for young audiences. Ole Kampovski Head of Children and Youth Department at NDR, added: 'Gifted is a great story full of friendship, mystery and adventures. It is a program, I am sure, our audience will enjoy a lot. 'NDR is very happy to produce such a marvellous show together with our great partners Black Camel Pictures, Media Valley, CBBC and OneGate.' News of the upcoming series comes after it was announced that the Harry Potter TV show could feature legendary British actor Bill Nighy. The series is 'set to cast' actor Bill Nighy to star in the new episodes after the actor, 75, was secretly approached by bosses working on the HBO series, which went into production in August. It's understood that Bill has taken part in screen tests to play a Hogwarts potions master role. The news comes after the Love Actually star agreed to voice a character for the new Harry Potter audio series. An insider said: 'It has been very "hush-hush", but Bill was thrilled to take part in screen tests for the role last month.' They continued to The Sun: 'He wants it, the Potter production team want it, and now it's a waiting game until contracts are signed. It will be a real coup to have Bill join a stellar cast.' 'I’m always grateful when asked to play academics, having not been further educated myself.' Bill previously starred in the original movies, playing minister for magic Rufus Scrimgeour. Dominic McLaughlin has bagged the role of Harry Potter, as Arabella Stanton will play Hermoine Granger and Alastair Stout will portray Ron Weasley. Additional cast sees Rory Wilmot set play Neville Longbottom, Amos Kitson as Dudley Dursley, Louise Brealey as Madam Rolanda Hooch, and Anton Lesser - best known for his role as Qyburn in Game Of Thrones - as Garrick Ollivander. Gifted is set to air on CBBC and iPlayer from November 24. Image via HBO By Remus Noronha Published Nov 5, 2025 Remus is a writer, editor, journalist, and author with an eye for detail and an extremely active imagination. He is an enthusiast of everything to do with the graphic medium, whether it's Western comics and their adaptations or manga and anime. Remus is also the author of the sci-fantasy novel Once Upon a Time in Hyperspace and several works of short fiction in the mystery, comedy, and horror genres. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap In January 2021, it was announced that a series adaptation of the Harry Potter novels was in the works for HBO. The news surprised very few; after all, the Harry Potter franchise is a multi-billion-dollar institution that includes seven hit novels, eight successful mainline movies, and a somewhat less successful trilogy of prequel films. However, reactions to this upcoming series reboot have been rather mixed. With the enduring popularity of the books and movie adaptations, a series adaptation of the Wizarding World does seem rather unnecessary, and it has even faced accusations of being a blatant cash grab. (There's also the J.K. Rowling of it all ...) Of course, since the show isn’t due to premiere until 2027 at the earliest, we won’t know any time soon if the series is actually worthwhile. In the meantime, there are still plenty of interesting, original fantasy shows out there that are. So, without further ado, here’s a look at some amazing fantasy series you should watch instead of Harry Potter . 8 ‘His Dark Materials’ (2019 - 2022) Lyra holding the compass in His Dark Materials. Image via HBO Based on Philip Pullman ’s book series of the same name, His Dark Materials is a fantasy drama series starring Dafne Keene as Lyra, a young girl from a world where souls manifest outside the body as animal companions and a corrupt theocracy rules the world. Set across multiple worlds, the show follows Lyra as she tries to find her missing friend, uncovering a conspiracy related to an invisible cosmic substance with strange properties called Dust. Besides Keene, the series also stars Ruth Wilson , Anne-Marie Duff , James McAvoy , Clarke Peters , James Cosmo , and more. A masterful adaptation of a complex, intricately crafted novel series, His Dark Materials earned critical and audience acclaim for all three of its seasons, receiving special praise for its visuals, music, and faithfulness to the source material (which sets it apart from the critically panned 2007 movie adaptation, The Golden Compass ). With spectacular performances, a great story, and gorgeous special effects, it’s an immersive series set in a multiverse of strange and fascinating phenomena. The show has earned several accolades and is widely regarded as one of the best fantasy shows of the 21st century so far. 7 ‘Lockwood & Co.’ (2023) Lockwood & Co's three protagonists (Ruby Stokes, Cameron Chapman, Ali Hadji-Heshmati) stopping short and staring ahead. Image Via Netflix Developed by Joe Cornish , Lockwood & Co. is a British supernatural detective thriller show adapted from Jonathan Stroud ’s eponymous book series. Set in an alternate version of present-day Britain, where the populace is plagued by deadly ghosts, the show stars Ruby Stokes as Lucy Carlyle, a gifted teenager who runs away to London and joins the titular agency run by two boys, Anthony Lockwood ( Cameron Chapman ) and George Karim ( Ali Hadji-Heshmati ). Ivanno Jeremiah , Jack Bandeira , Bronwyn James , Louise Brealey , and more appear in recurring roles. Lockwood & Co. ’s eight-episode first season was released on Netflix in 2023, earning near-universal acclaim and becoming the service’s number one show in 18 countries. Despite its popularity, however, the series was canceled after just one season. While that does mean that the show is tragically short, it’s still one of the best fantasy series on the service, with a charming and intelligent story, well-crafted characters, and an engaging supernatural mystery at its heart. 6 ‘Shadow and Bone’ (2021 - 2023) Adapted from Leigh Bardugo ’s Grishaverse young adult fantasy novels, Shadow and Bone is a fantasy drama series developed by Eric Heisserer . The show stars Jessie Mei Li as orphan cartographer Alina Starkov, who discovers an immensely important magical ability and becomes the target of multiple factions who seek to use her powers for their own agendas. Ben Barnes , Archie Renaux , Freddy Carter , Amita Suman , Kit Young , and more appear in supporting roles. Shadow and Bone is an ambitious adaptation that combines elements of Bardugo’s Shadow and Bone trilogy and Six of Crows duology to craft a fascinating new story, which earned positive reviews from critics and fans. A well-crafted YA fantasy, the series has some amazing world-building and great performances, bringing Bardugo’s Grishaverse to life in a way that feels familiar to fans of the books but also new enough to still be an engaging watch. While it has faced its share of valid criticisms, especially due to the show’s simplistic portrayal of racism and its general handling of race relations, the series has developed a sizable fanbase, and it’s easily one of Netflix’s most underrated fantasy shows (and one that was canceled far too soon). 5 ‘Stranger Things’ (2016 - 2025) Millie Bobby Brown in Stranger Things 4 Image via Netflix One of the most celebrated fantasy shows of the past decade, Stranger Things is a genre-bending coming-of-age series created by the Duffer Brothers . Set in the 1980s, the show revolves around the small town of Hawkins, Indiana, which becomes the epicenter of supernatural forces and secret government experiments involving an alternate dimension known as the Upside Down. The series features a star-studded cast that includes Winona Ryder , David Harbour , Finn Wolfhard , Millie Bobby Brown , Gaten Matarazzo , Caleb McLaughlin , Natalia Dyer , Noah Schnapp , Sadie Sink , Joe Keery , and more. Easily one of Netflix’s most popular original productions, Stranger Things is a highly successful series that has earned near-universal acclaim and developed a massive global fan following. It’s a nostalgic mystery adventure show that draws on classic horror stories and iconic elements of '80s pop culture to create a mindblowing story of drama, sci-fi, fantasy, and horror, anchored by the performances of its talented ensemble. The series has received several accolades, including 10 Emmy Award nominations, and expanded into a multimedia franchise with spin-offs, tie-in books, games, an Olivier Award-nominated play, and more. 4 ‘Percy Jackson & the Olympians’ (2023 - Present) Walker Scobell, Aryan Simhadri, Leah Sava Jeffries standing together in Percy Jackson and the Olympians. Image via Disney+ Based on the eponymous novel series by Rick Riordan , Percy Jackson & the Olympians is a fantasy adventure show created by Riordan and Jonathan E. Steinberg . Walker Scobell stars in the titular role as Percy Jackson, a young boy who discovers that he’s the demigod son of the Olympian deity Poseidon, just in time to be accused of stealing an important magical artifact. The show also stars Leah Sava Jeffries and Aryan Simhadri as lead characters, with Dior Goodjohn , Charlie Bushnell , Virginia Kull , Glynn Turman , Jason Mantzoukas , and more in supporting roles. The Percy Jackson novels were originally adapted as movies in the 2010s, which were widely panned by critics and the franchise’s fans, but their failure spurred the creation of this series adaptation with the franchise creator at the helm. The result is a series that has been widely acclaimed as a much more faithful adaptation that fully captures the charm and wonder of its source material. Praised for its narrative, worldbuilding, and performances, the series has had two seasons so far, with a third on the way, and it has earned multiple accolades, including eight Children's and Family Emmy Awards out of 16 nominations. 3 ‘Wednesday’ (2022 - Present) Jenna Ortega as Wednesday Addams with Thing on her shoulder outside by trees in Wednesday. Image via Netflix A modern reimagining of Charles Addams ’ The Addams Family , Wednesday is a gothic mystery comedy show starring Jenna Ortega as Wednesday Addams. Created by Alfred Gough and Miles Millar , and executive-produced by Tim Burton , the show follows Wednesday’s adventures at Nevermore Academy, a boarding school for the creepy, kooky, and magically gifted, where she learns to control her latent psychic abilities while facing off against a supernatural serial killer, ancient conspiracies, and evil masterminds. Emma Myers , Hunter Doohan , Christina Ricci , Gwendoline Christie , Riki Lindhome , Moosa Mostafa , and more star in supporting roles. One of the biggest fantasy hits of the 2020s, Wednesday premiered to critical and audience acclaim in November 2022, becoming Netflix’s second-most-watched English-language series within three weeks. A second season premiered three years later, in 2025, and the show has been renewed for a third outing. With great performances, cinematography, music, and special effects, it’s a highly entertaining show with a huge global fanbase that has won multiple honors, including four Emmy Awards. 2 ‘Legacies’ (2018 - 2021) Image via The CW The third entry in The Vampire Diaries Universe and a sequel to The Originals , Legacies is a fantasy drama series created by Julie Plec , who also co-created the franchise. Danielle Rose Russell stars as Hope Mikaelson, the 17-year-old daughter of The Originals ’ lead character Klaus Mikaelson ( Joseph Morgan ). Descended from a powerful line of witches, werewolves, and vampires, Hope learns to master her abilities, forms new relationships, and confronts various supernatural threats at the Salvatore Boarding School for the Young and Gifted alongside other children of supernatural beings. Besides Russell, the show stars Aria Shahghasemi , Kaylee Bryant , Jenny Boyd , Matt Davis , and more in significant roles, with multiple stars from The Originals and The Vampire Diaries making guest appearances. The Vampire Diaries Universe may have started as a book adaptation, but it’s since developed into a massive world of its own, and Legacies is arguably the best new entry point into the franchise for young viewers. The show populates its Harry Potter -esque magical school setting with interesting characters and great dramatic storylines, creating a fascinating and binge-worthy world for you to explore. The series aired four seasons on The CW before its conclusion in 2022 and has earned largely favorable reviews from both critics and longtime franchise fans. 1 ‘The Magicians’ (2015 - 2020) Quentin (Jason Ralph), Alice (Olivia Taylor Dudley), and Penny (Arjun Gupta), in the Brakebills library in 'The Magicians.' Image via Syfy Adapted from Lev Grossman ’s titular trilogy, The Magicians is a fantasy series developed by Sera Gamble and John McNamara . The show stars Jason Ralph as Quentin Coldwater, a graduate student who enrolls at Brakebills University for Magical Pedagogy, where he learns that his favorite childhood book series is based on real truths that threaten the world. Meanwhile, his childhood friend Julia ( Stella Maeve ), who is denied entry to the school, finds her own path to magic that opens the way for more dangers. The show also features Olivia Taylor Dudley , Hale Appleman , Arjun Gupta , Summer Bishil , Rick Worthy , Jade Tailor , Brittany Curran , and Trevor Einhorn in key roles. A mature story set in a school of wizardry, both the Magicians Trilogy novels and the show have been favorably compared to the Harry Potter books , and it’s a great watch for grown-up Potterheads looking for a new world of wonders and weirdness. All five seasons of The Magicians were nominated for Saturn Awards, and it earned favorable reviews from critics and fans throughout its run. A visually stunning, well-acted, and well-written fantasy drama with a dark sense of humor, the show follows a likable cast of characters on mindbending adventures that are intelligent, unpredictable, and delightfully meta. Easily one of Netflix’s most popular original productions, Stranger Things is a highly successful series that has earned near-universal acclaim and developed a massive global fan following. It’s a nostalgic mystery adventure show that draws on classic horror stories and iconic elements of '80s pop culture to create a mindblowing story of drama, sci-fi, fantasy, and horror, anchored by the performances of its talented ensemble. The series has received several accolades, including 10 Emmy Award nominations, and expanded into a multimedia franchise with spin-offs, tie-in books, games, an Olivier Award-nominated play, and more. 4 ‘Percy Jackson & the Olympians’ (2023 - Present) Walker Scobell, Aryan Simhadri, Leah Sava Jeffries standing together in Percy Jackson and the Olympians. Image via Disney+ Based on the eponymous novel series by Rick Riordan , Percy Jackson & the Olympians is a fantasy adventure show created by Riordan and Jonathan E. Walker Scobell stars in the titular role as Percy Jackson, a young boy who discovers that he’s the demigod son of the Olympian deity Poseidon, just in time to be accused of stealing an important magical artifact. The show also stars Leah Sava Jeffries and Aryan Simhadri as lead characters, with Dior Goodjohn , Charlie Bushnell , Virginia Kull , Glynn Turman , Jason Mantzoukas , and more in supporting roles. The Percy Jackson novels were originally adapted as movies in the 2010s, which were widely panned by critics and the franchise’s fans, but their failure spurred the creation of this series adaptation with the franchise creator at the helm. The result is a series that has been widely acclaimed as a much more faithful adaptation that fully captures the charm and wonder of its source material. Praised for its narrative, worldbuilding, and performances, the series has had two seasons so far, with a third on the way, and it has earned multiple accolades, including eight Children's and Family Emmy Awards out of 16 nominations. 3 ‘Wednesday’ (2022 - Present) Jenna Ortega as Wednesday Addams with Thing on her shoulder outside by trees in Wednesday. Image via Netflix A modern reimagining of Charles Addams ’ The Addams Family , Wednesday is a gothic mystery comedy show starring Jenna Ortega as Wednesday Addams. Created by Alfred Gough and Miles Millar , and executive-produced by Tim Burton , the show follows Wednesday’s adventures at Nevermore Academy, a boarding school for the creepy, kooky, and magically gifted, where she learns to control her latent psychic abilities while facing off against a supernatural serial killer, ancient conspiracies, and evil masterminds. Emma Myers , Hunter Doohan , Christina Ricci , Gwendoline Christie , Riki Lindhome , Moosa Mostafa , and more star in supporting roles. One of the biggest fantasy hits of the 2020s, Wednesday premiered to critical and audience acclaim in November 2022, becoming Netflix’s second-most-watched English-language series within three weeks. A second season premiered three years later, in 2025, and the show has been renewed for a third outing. With great performances, cinematography, music, and special effects, it’s a highly entertaining show with a huge global fanbase that has won multiple honors, including four Emmy Awards. 2 ‘Legacies’ (2018 - 2021) Image via The CW The third entry in The Vampire Diaries Universe and a sequel to The Originals , Legacies is a fantasy drama series created by Julie Plec , who also co-created the franchise. Danielle Rose Russell stars as Hope Mikaelson, the 17-year-old daughter of The Originals ’ lead character Klaus Mikaelson ( Joseph Morgan ). Descended from a powerful line of witches, werewolves, and vampires, Hope learns to master her abilities, forms new relationships, and confronts various supernatural threats at the Salvatore Boarding School for the Young and Gifted alongside other children of supernatural beings. Besides Russell, the show stars Aria Shahghasemi , Kaylee Bryant , Jenny Boyd , Matt Davis , and more in significant roles, with multiple stars from The Originals and The Vampire Diaries making guest appearances. The Vampire Diaries Universe may have started as a book adaptation, but it’s since developed into a massive world of its own, and Legacies is arguably the best new entry point into the franchise for young viewers. The show populates its Harry Potter -esque magical school setting with interesting characters and great dramatic storylines, creating a fascinating and binge-worthy world for you to explore. The series aired four seasons on The CW before its conclusion in 2022 and has earned largely favorable reviews from both critics and longtime franchise fans. 1 ‘The Magicians’ (2015 - 2020) Quentin (Jason Ralph), Alice (Olivia Taylor Dudley), and Penny (Arjun Gupta), in the Brakebills library in 'The Magicians. ' Image via Syfy Adapted from Lev Grossman ’s titular trilogy, The Magicians is a fantasy series developed by Sera Gamble and John McNamara. The show stars Jason Ralph as Quentin Coldwater, a graduate student who enrolls at Brakebills University for Magical Pedagogy, where he learns that his favorite childhood book series is based on real truths that threaten the world. Meanwhile, his childhood friend Julia ( Stella Maeve ), who is denied entry to the school, finds her own path to magic that opens the way for more dangers. The show also features Olivia Taylor Dudley , Hale Appleman , Arjun Gupta , Summer Bishil , Rick Worthy , Jade Tailor , Brittany Curran , and Trevor Einhorn in key roles. A mature story set in a school of wizardry, both the Magicians Trilogy novels and the show have been favorably compared to the Harry Potter books , and it’s a great watch for grown-up Potterheads looking for a new world of wonders and weirdness. All five seasons of The Magicians were nominated for Saturn Awards, and it earned favorable reviews from critics and fans throughout its run. A visually stunning, well-acted, and well-written fantasy drama with a dark sense of humor, the show follows a likable cast of characters on mindbending adventures that are intelligent, unpredictable, and delightfully meta. Published Mon, 10 Nov 2025 15:07:04 -0600 by Ray Flook | Comments Article Summary Outlander Season 8 premieres March 6, 2026, marking the beginning of the epic series' final journey. Caitríona Balfe and Sam Heughan return as Claire and Jamie Fraser for the show's last season on STARZ. The teaser retraces seven seasons and drops major hints about upcoming storylines and challenges. Season 8 sees Fraser’s Ridge in turmoil, with secrets and new arrivals threatening the family's unity. Back in September, STARZ released an official teaser for the eighth and final season of Showrunner Matthew B. Roberts ' Caitríona Balfe (Claire Fraser) and Sam Heughan (Jamie Fraser)-starring Outlander that retraced the seven-season journey before dropping some interesting clues about what's still to come. Now, we're getting a look at the official key art for Season 8, announcing that the series will return on Friday, March 6th, 2026 (with new episodes available to stream weekly on Fridays only on the STARZ app and all STARZ streaming & on-demand platforms). In addition to Balfe and Heughan, the series stars Sophie Skelton as Brianna MacKenzie, Richard Rankin as Roger MacKenzie, John Bell as Young Ian, David Berry as Lord John Grey, Charles Vandervaart as William Ransom, Izzy Meikle-Small as Rachel Hunter, and Joey Phillips as Denzell Hunter. Outlander Season 8 Key Art, Image IDs: OLS8_080824_1555, shutterstock_2299799851, shutterstock_196332797, shutterstock_1854851881 As Season Eight begins, Jamie and Claire soon find the war has followed them home to Fraser's Ridge, now a thriving settlement that has grown and flourished in their absence. With new arrivals and changes made during their years away, the Frasers are confronted with the question of what they are willing to sacrifice for the place they call home and, more importantly, what they would sacrifice to stay together. While the Frasers keep a united front against outside intruders, family secrets finally coming to light threaten to tear them apart from the inside. Although they've left the war for America's freedom behind, their fight for Fraser's Ridge has only just begun. Matthew B. Roberts, Ronald D. Moore, Maril Davis, Toni Graphia, Luke Schelhaas, Andy Harries, Jim Kohlberg, Caitríona Balfe , and Sam Heughan executive produce the STARZ series. Produced by Tall Ship Productions, Left Bank Pictures, and Story Mining & Supply Company (in association with Sony Pictures Television), Outlander is inspired by Diana Gabaldon 's international best-selling books, which have sold an estimated 50 million copies worldwide (with all nine of the books gracing the New York Times best-seller list ). Georgia Oakley, who won a People’s Choice Award recently at Venice for her feature directorial debut “Blue Jean,” directed the film from a script by author Diana Reid. The film also stars Esmé Creed-Miles, George MacKay, Caitríona Balfe, Fiona Shaw and Frank Dillane. Tim Bevan and Eric Fellner of Working Title Films produced “Sense and Sensibility” alongside India Flint of November Pictures and Jo Wallett. Originally published anonymously with the byline reading, “By a Lady,” Austen’s “Sense and Sensibility” established her as a literary force and follows sisters Elinor (Edgar-Jones) and Marianne Dashwood (Creed-Miles), opposites in their emotional approach, as they navigate love, loss and financial uncertainty amid the societal expectations of 18th century England. Balfe, known for her starring role in “Outlander,” is set to play the Dashwood matriarch. Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet starred as the Dashwood sisters in the critically-acclaimed 1995 feature film, which also featured the late Alan Rickman and Hugh Grant. The film earned seven Academy Award nominations, nabbing a Best Adapted Screenplay win for Thompson, who wrote the script for the Ang Lee-directed picture. Focus has worldwide rights on the movie and UPI will handle international distribution for the studio. When is the new Sense and Sensibility release date? Sense and Sensibility will release in theaters in the United States on September 11, 2026, and will then release in the United Kingdom on September 25, 2026. The film, which is based on the iconic novel of the same name from Jane Austen, will be the latest in a long line of adaptations based around the novel. Edgar-Jones will lead the film as Elinor Dashwood, with the rest of the cast set to include Esmé Creed-Miles, George MacKay, Caitríona Balfe, Fiona Shaw, Frank Dillane, Herbert Nordrum, and Bodhi Rae Breathnatch. The movie will be directed by Georgia Oakley (Blue Jean), from a script written by Diana Reid. Described as a fresh take on the Jane Austen classic, the upcoming adaptation will be directed by Georgia Oakley (Blue Jean) from a screenplay written by bestselling author Diana Reid. The story follows the lives of the Dashwood sisters and their mother, who are forced to move out of their family estate following the death of their father. The project is produced by Tim Bevan and Eric Fellner of Working Title Films, alongside India Flint of November Pictures and Jo Wallett. Besides the Sense and Sensibility movie, their are more Jane Austen adaptations on the way, including Netflix’s upcoming series and modern remake of Austen’s popular Pride and Prejudice novel. Prior to the upcoming projects, Austen’s novel was famously adapted in 1995 with Keira Knightley and Matthew Macfadyen leading the film’s cast as Elizabeth Bennett and Mr. Darcy, respectively. Meanwhile, after an emotional family reunion, the MacKenzies needed to decide where and when to settle next, and a haunting cliffhanger left fans questioning the true fate of Claire and Jamie’s first daughter, Faith. With new arrivals and changes made during their years away, the Frasers are confronted with the question of what they are willing to sacrifice for the place they call home and, more importantly, what they would sacrifice to stay together. While the Frasers keep a united front against outside intruders, family secrets finally coming to light threaten to tear them apart from the inside. Although they’ve left the war for America’s freedom behind, their fight for Fraser’s Ridge has only just begun. The cast includes Daisy Edgar-Jones, Esmé Creed-Miles, Caitríona Balfe, Frank Dillane, Herbert Nordrum, Bodhi Rae Breathnach, George MacKay, and Fiona Shaw. Focus Features has announced that Sense and Sensibility will be released in U.S. theaters on September 11, 2026, followed by a September 26 theatrical debut in the U.K. This comes after Shaw, who plays Mrs. Jennings, provided an update earlier in November that filming had wrapped on the adaptation. The Jane Austen book , which was the iconic author's first published novel, follows sisters Elinor and Marianne Dashwood after the death of their father and as they navigate romantic relationships. Edgar-Jones plays Elinor, Creed-Miles plays Marianne, and Outlander 's Balfe plays their mother, Mrs. Dashwood, in the upcoming adaptation. Georgia Oakley directs the new take on Sense and Sensibility , the first of many to tackle Austen's source material. The 1995 movie directed by Ang Lee and starring Emma Thompson and Kate Winslet as Elinor and Marianne is widely considered to be one of the all-time best Jane Austen adaptations , holding a 97% critical score and 90% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. 1995's Sense and Sensibility received seven Academy Award nominations. Thompson was not only nominated for her performance, but also won an Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay. This adaptation was also a massive box office hit, grossing nearly $135 million worldwide against an estimated budget of $16 million. Working Title's Tim Bevan and Eric Fellner are among the producers for 2026's Sense and Sensibility . Focus Features and Working Title have collaborated on several feature film adaptations of Austen's work in the past, from 2005's Pride and Prejudice and 2020's Emma . This version of Pride and Prejudice received four Academy Award nominations, including Keira Knightley for Best Actress, Best Achievement in Art Direction, Best Achievement in Costume Design, and Best Original Score. These past collaborations bode well for the new Sense and Sensibility , as does how well some of Daisy Edgar-Jones' movies have performed at the box office in recent years. 2024's Twisters made $372 million worldwide, $276 million of which was from the domestic box office. Against a reported budget of $24 million, 2022's Where the Crawdads Sing earned $144 million worldwide.
