The picture above features Johnson and McCarrol taking the streets of Toronto, ready for another adventure. Get all the details about Nirvanna the Band the Show the Movie in our exclusive look. 'Hamnet' Release Date: November 26, 2025 The winner of the People's Choice Award at the 50th Toronto International Film Festival, Chloé Zhao’s Hamnet is already lining up to be a serious contender come next year's Academy Awards. Rumored to earn nominations in several categories, the movie's lead Jessie Buckley , who stars alongside the ever-brilliant Paul Mescal , is currently the frontrunner to not just earn a nomination for Best Actress but to win the prize altogether. Ahead of the movie's limited theatrical release on November 26, with a nationwide release on December 12, Collider debuted the above exclusive image as part of our Winter Preview Event, giving fans a glimpse of Mescal's take on The Bard, as well as exclusive quotes available to read via the link below. A synopsis for Hamnet reads: "From Academy Award® winning writer/director Chloé Zhao, HAMNET tells the powerful story of love and loss that inspired the creation of Shakespeare’s timeless masterpiece, Hamlet. " Get all the details about Hamnet in our exclusive look. 'Bel-Air' Season 4 Release Date: November 24, 2025 Bel-Air-Final-Season A beloved spin-off is coming to an end soon, after building on the legacy of the 1990 hit series, The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air. As Bel-Air gears towards its Season 4 release, audiences can anticipate Will Smith ( Jabari Banks ) navigating the excitement of senior year, while also feeling daunted by what the future holds for him once he is out of the high school halls. In our exclusive look at Season 4, we see Hilary Banks ( Coco Janks ) clapping with a smile on. Get all the details about Bel-Air Season 4 in our exclusive preview. "They have only 12 hours to navigate the lethal streets amidst a citywide riot, pay a large ransom, and frame a dangerous criminal organization," the synopsis reads. Director James Nunn 's Wildcat , scheduled to release on November 25, stars Beckinsale alongside the likes of Lewis Tan ( Mortal Kombat franchise), Charles Dance ( Game of Thrones ), Tom Bennett ( House of the Dragon ), Alice Krige ( Star Trek: First Contact ), Edmund Kingsley ( The Witcher ), and Matt Willis ( Missing You ). Ahead of the movie's release, Collider debuted not just an exclusive image and clip, but also a selection of quotes, available to read via the link below. Get all the details about Wildcat in our exclusive look. ‘Father Mother Sister Brother’ Release Date: December 24, 2025 Father-Mother-Sister-Brother_©-Vague-Notion-2024_Frederick-Elmes Almost ten years ago, Adam Driver and director Jim Jarmusch collaborated on the critically acclaimed Paterson. As part of Collider’s Exclusive Winter Preview Event, we debuted a brand-new image from the upcoming release, scheduled for Christmas Eve. Get all the details about A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms in our exclusive look. As can be seen in the image above, which debuted as part of Collider's Exclusive Winter Preview Event, the danger of deadly scarabs are putting the life of a surfer at risk, with it confirmed that these creatures will appear frequently throughout the second season. Get all the details about Monarch: Legacy of Monsters Season 2 in our exclusive look. Directed by Sam Raimi , this survival thriller follows Linda and Bradley, two work colleagues who make it out alive from a plane crash. The upcoming episodes will have new additions to the cast, including Matthew Lillard , Jeanine Mason , and Wes Chatham. Apple TV Morgan Cormack Published: Saturday, 15 November 2025 at 9:00 am Subscribe to Radio Times: 10 weeks for £10, including the Christmas edition Share on facebook Share on twitter Share on pinterest Share on reddit Email to a friend As we continue veering to the anticipated finale of The Morning Show season 4 , we can rest easy in the fact that the candid TV drama is in fact returning for more. Ad It was announced back in September ahead of season 4's release that Apple had renewed the series for a fifth instalment. The early renewal didn't come as too much of a surprise to fans, seeing as Apple TV had done precisely the same thing ahead of season 3's release too. “The Morning Show has been a standout from the very start, debuting as one of the flagship series on Apple TV+. It’s been incredibly rewarding to see it not only entertain but also resonate with audiences worldwide,” said Matt Cherniss, head of programming at Apple TV+. He continued: “Thanks to the outstanding cast and creative team — led by Jennifer, Reese, Charlotte and Mimi — The Morning Show continues to deliver addictively entertaining and provocative stories that we’ve all come to love. We’re excited for viewers to experience the next chapter of this Emmy-winning drama.” But just when will season 5 of The Morning Show be released and who will star? Read on for everything we know so far. The Morning Show season 5 release date speculation Apple TV has not yet announced a release date for the fifth season of The Morning Show so we'll just have to wait and see when new episodes are set to come out. However, the show has usually followed a pattern that means seasons are released every couple of years. So, that could very well mean that season 5 will be released in 2027 . The Morning Show season 5 cast: Who will return? Reese Witherspoon as Bradley Jackson and Jennifer Aniston as Alex Levy walk the streets of Manhattan in The Morning Show season 4 poster. Apple TV+ Despite being given an official series renewal, there has been no news of who will be returning to star in the fifth season of The Morning Show. We can imagine that leading stars Reese Witherspoon and Jennifer Aniston will return to helm the series, along with most of the familiar faces of the previous season. text: Reese Witherspoon learns shocking career fact about costar Karen Pittman Home Latest News World Sports Entertainment Science Royal Trending Health Videos Technology Home Latest News World Sports Entertainment Science Royal Trending Health Videos Technology Donald Trump 3I/ATLAS AI Cristiano Ronaldo Kate Middleton Elon Musk Taylor Swift Hollywood Reese Witherspoon learns shocking career fact about costar Karen Pittman Reese Witherspoon's ‘The Morning Show’ costar Karen Pittman feels 'healed' through 'acting' By The News Digital October 29, 2025 Reese Witherspoon learned something new about her longtime costar Karen Pittman, and her reaction said it all. While speaking at Hello Sunshine’s Shine Away event in mid-October, Witherspoon joined Pittman and Mariska Hargitay for a conversation titled “Connecting Passion to Purpose.” Though all three women are known for their work in film and TV, Witherspoon was surprised to hear that Pittman once worked in a completely different field. “You really did work in finance?” Witherspoon asked, sounding stunned. “I did work in finance,” Pittman confirmed, prompting Witherspoon to exclaim, “How are we just learning this right now?” Pittman reminded her The Morning Show costar that they’ve known each other for years. “I worked in finance, we've only worked together for seven years,” she joked, while Witherspoon repeated, “I had no idea!” The And Just Like That… alum shared that her finance career began mostly as “a cash grab kind of a job,” but eventually she realized money wasn’t the answer. She explained that leaving finance helped her chase something more fulfilling. Pittman said acting became a powerful outlet for her, helping her work through emotional experiences. “Acting became that for me, a way to manage my hurt and my pain,” she said. But as her journey continued, she noted that unresolved wounds can also get in the way. “You get to a certain place in your work though, and that trauma, that woundedness becomes — it becomes a crippling obstacle to actually doing good work. And so you have to go back in and find another way.” “I just think that acting in so many ways has healed me,” she continued. “It's led me to nowhere but back inward to myself in a lot of ways when I've allowed it to.” When asked who inspires her to keep pursuing her passion, Pittman’s answer was simple and confident. “I can do it. Me,” she said. She shared that people, especially women, are often taught to put themselves second, and unlearning that is a brave act. She added that her mother and daughter motivate her, along with those who see themselves in her work. Pittman acknowledges that being a Black actress comes with responsibility, even if she says it’s “teeny” rather than overwhelming. She knows viewers find representation in the characters she has played, including Mia Jordan, Dawn Edwards, and Naya Wallace, and that gives her another reason to keep going. For Pittman, the encouragement of loved ones also matters. She said she finds purpose “looking at the people who love me, who insist that I deserve the best.” Witherspoon may not have known about Pittman’s former life in finance, but it’s clear her journey into acting has shaped her in meaningful ways, both personally and creatively. Search site Submit search Subscribe Newsletter Advertise News & City Arts & Entertainment Food & Drink Life & Style Events Sports Top Professionals Awards Travel Newsletter Sign Up Advertise News & City Arts & Entertainment Food & Drink Life & Style Events Sports Top Professionals Awards Travel Search Search site Submit search Honoree Jamie Lee Curtis and Presenter Jane Fonda Get Political at WIF Honors Gala Plus, Kristen Wiig is named an ‘Icon’ and Maude Apatow received the 20th WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award Jasmin Rosemberg • November 7, 2025 Jane Fonda presents Jamie Lee Curtis the Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award at the 2025 WIF Honors presented by Max Mara Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF “For the last five years, I’ve been lucky enough to present the Women In Film Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award,” began Jane Fonda after receiving a standing ovation in the Beverly Hilton ballroom at the WIF Honors event presented by Max Mara on Nov. 6. “[I present it] to a woman in the entertainment industry who demonstrates brave commitment to humanitarian issues, and is woke,” she said, to laughs. She pulled back her maroon Max Mara blazer to reveal a black T-shirt with the word, “resist.” Fonda continued: “I realized, given today’s reality, humanitarianism and empathy are essential forms of resistance. … It’s at the heart of what we do in our profession, empathy. And you know what else is at the heart of what we do? The First Amendment. Our profession, like all art forms, can’t exist without freedom of expression. It’s the bedrock of democracy, and it’s being taken away from us. And that’s why, on Oct. 1, we launched the Committee for the First Amendment .” Fonda clarified the Committee was re-launched, as it existed in the ’70’s and ’80s, when her father was a member. “But dig this,” she said. “That was about one small part of government robbing us of our First Amendment. Right now, it’s the entire federal government. It is far, far worse than what existed back in the ’40s and ’50s. And so, we have to do something about that.” Then she praised the recipient of this year’s Jane Fonda Humanitarian Award. “Jamie Lee Curtis and I have a few things in common,” Fonda said. “We’re both children of major movie stars and we made our own way quite successfully in their business. And we’re both late bloomers — which is okay. It moves me very deeply to see how Jamie uses her skills and her remarkable ego-less courage as an actor. … And last January, when the fires were burning and our hearts were breaking, I heard Jamie Lee Curtis had given a million dollars to the fire department and it made me cry.” Fonda added how Curtis had also raised millions of dollars for Children’s Hospital L.A., and has used her voice for addiction and trans rights. When she took the stage, Curtis also spoke about government. “I heard it today that she is retiring from public service, and I thought this Women In Film crowd could just give Nancy Pelosi a loud [round of applause]. … What an example to me of a life of service!” She also professed: “I am most excited to stand here two days after the repudiation of the authoritative regime. The election of these two beautiful women to governorships.” Curtis thanked her presenter. “Jane Fonda, I have watched you in wonder and shock and awe, at the way that you walk through the world as an artist, as an activist and as a disruptor in residence.” She noted that she joined the Committee of the First Amendment. Credit: hoto by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Then she recalled the birth of her activism. “My mother, the late, great, Janet Leigh,” Curtis said, getting tearful, “was an actress with an impressive career. But she knew there was much more to be done with fame.” She described how a group of seven women whose husbands were in entertainment (including Gloria Franks and Jeanne Martin) came together to use their positions to help children and form SHARE (Share Happily And Reap Endlessly), which her mother joined. “For 70 years, the group has raised over $70 million for children,” said Curtis, who has fond memories of helping in their events as a child. Getting emotional again, she added, “I know that my mother would be so very proud that her life and her work made an impact on mine.” Curtis told the audience how, on Dec. 12, Disney is releasing Ella McKay. “It’s about the rise of an idealistic young woman,” she said, “but it’s also a movie about politics.” She ended by citing the last line of the narration of the movie, which she stars in. “‘There is no opposite word for trauma, but hope comes close,'” Curtis read. “And today, I feel hope.” WIF CEO Kirsten Schaffer also acknowledged today’s difficult climate. “There is no doubt that there are people in positions of great power who would like to erase us: Erase our impact, silence our voices, diminish our power, keep us quiet and small and ineffective,” she said. “But we are not small. We are seldom quiet. And we are definitely effective.” WIF’s mission is to advance equity and representation across the screen industries. The WIF Honors gala — which celebrates female storytellers and change-makers who are making their mark on culture through their art and advocacy — raises funds for WIF’s education, career development and advocacy programs. Other sponsors of this year’s event included e.l.f. Cosmetics, Amazon MGM Studios, Apple TV, Delta Air Lines, Disney, Los Angeles County Supervisor Lindsey P. Horvath, Netflix and STARZ #TakeTheLead. Karen Pittman, wearing Max Mara, Davida Lara, Regina King, wearing Max Mara, Roda Ahmed, Mara Brock Akil, wearing Max Mara, and Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Next, Karen Pittman honored Forever ’s Mara Brock Akil, Judy Blume (who accepted via video) and Regina King with the Crystal Award for Advocacy in TV. “What woman has not read Judy Blume?” said King during a conversation. “You become a writer as a reader first, and I devoured every book that she had,” added Akil. Maria Bello, the first recipient of the WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award, called up other past recipients — Lili Reinhart (2022), Elizabeth Debicki (2019) and Zoey Deutch (2017) — in celebration of the award’s 20th anniversary. Elizabeth Debicki, Lili Reinhart, Maria Giulia Prezioso Maramotti, Maude Apatow, Zoey Deutch and Maria Bello, all wearing Max Mara with Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF attend the 2025 WIF Honors presented by Max Mara Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Then, Maude Apatow received the 20th WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award from Maria Giulia Prezioso Maramotti, whose grandfather founded Max Mara 75 years ago. Max Mara has supported the WIF Honors event since the beginning, and dressed 2025 attendees included King, Curtis, Fonda, Pittman, Apatow, Mara Brock Akil, Gabrielle Nadig, Atsuko Okatsuka, Janicza Bravo, Reinhart, Deutch, Debicki, Bello, Jurnee Smollett, Leslie Mann, Maggie Kang and Beth Reisgraf. “When I was 10, I read Are You There, God? It’s Me Margaret, ” said Apatow, shouting out Blume. “It was funny, angsty, truthful and made me fall in love with reading.” The actor and director then called out another female influence. “As a teenager, I got to watch a 20-something-year-old Lena Dunham write, direct, act and produce a truly groundbreaking show,” she said of Girls , produced by her father, Judd Apatow. She added, “But my favorite woman in film is my mom, Leslie Mann.” Francesca Amiker, Tessa Thompson, Dede Gardner and Gabrielle Nadig, wearing Max Mara, speak onstage at the 2025 WIF Honors Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Janicza Bravo presented the the Crystal Award for Advocacy in Film award to Hedda ’s Tessa Thompson, Nia DaCosta (not present), Dede Gardner and Gabrielle Nadig. Lastly, Kaia Gerber honored her Palm Royale co-star Kristen Wiig with the inaugural Icon Award. “Who better to receive it than my favorite scene partner?” Gerber said. “For seven years at SNL , Kristen showed us comedy could be completely unhinged and utterly ‘stupid’ — a word I learned from Kristen herself as one of the highest forms of praise in comedy — and also, somehow be simultaneously deeply human.” Kaia Gerber, Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF and Icon Award recipient Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Gerber continued, “When Bridesmaids came out, it was a revelation. … There is such truth and utter heartbreak behind [all of her characters].” She finished, “Tonight, we celebrate the woman who taught us that comedy is art, that chaos is beautiful, that sheer stupidity is not only encouraged but a necessity of life and that being unapologetically yourself might just be the most iconic move of all.” An emotional Wiig thanked Gerber, who she called “a lighthouse” on her show. “I’m fully overwhelmed,” she said. “This is my first time having to make a speech like this. I just kept thinking, ‘How did I get here?’ … I keep coming back to the people who said ‘yes’ to me before I had anything on my resume.” Wiig noted how her whole life changed when she joined The Groundlings. “That led to SNL ,” she said. She called out two men: Bridesmaids director Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow (who reached out to her and asked if she wanted to write something). “I certainly wouldn’t be up here getting an award from Women In Film if it weren’t for that movie,” she said of the project that changed her life. Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF But ultimately, she’s enjoyed collaborating with women and exploring female characters. “I just love stories about women,” Wiig said. “We’re so crazy! We’re complex. We talk to each other about how we age, and our sensitivities and our intuition. It’s a never-ending source of material. I want to keep going,” she pledged. “I want to keep telling stories about women, with women.” Wiig then offered everyone a challenge. “I still have things in my career that I really want to do — that I’m really scared to do,” she confessed. “And so I just thought, by chance, if everyone in this room has that thing that they’ve really wanted to do or really been scared to do — maybe we make like a collective pact with each other that we’re going to just do it, anyway.” Don’t keep it to yourself…share the love! Other sponsors of this year’s event included e. Cosmetics, Amazon MGM Studios, Apple TV, Delta Air Lines, Disney, Los Angeles County Supervisor Lindsey P. Horvath, Netflix and STARZ #TakeTheLead. Karen Pittman, wearing Max Mara, Davida Lara, Regina King, wearing Max Mara, Roda Ahmed, Mara Brock Akil, wearing Max Mara, and Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Next, Karen Pittman honored Forever ’s Mara Brock Akil, Judy Blume (who accepted via video) and Regina King with the Crystal Award for Advocacy in TV. “What woman has not read Judy Blume?” said King during a conversation. “You become a writer as a reader first, and I devoured every book that she had,” added Akil. Maria Bello, the first recipient of the WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award, called up other past recipients — Lili Reinhart (2022), Elizabeth Debicki (2019) and Zoey Deutch (2017) — in celebration of the award’s 20th anniversary. Elizabeth Debicki, Lili Reinhart, Maria Giulia Prezioso Maramotti, Maude Apatow, Zoey Deutch and Maria Bello, all wearing Max Mara with Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF attend the 2025 WIF Honors presented by Max Mara Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Then, Maude Apatow received the 20th WIF Max Mara Face of the Future Award from Maria Giulia Prezioso Maramotti, whose grandfather founded Max Mara 75 years ago. Max Mara has supported the WIF Honors event since the beginning, and dressed 2025 attendees included King, Curtis, Fonda, Pittman, Apatow, Mara Brock Akil, Gabrielle Nadig, Atsuko Okatsuka, Janicza Bravo, Reinhart, Deutch, Debicki, Bello, Jurnee Smollett, Leslie Mann, Maggie Kang and Beth Reisgraf. “When I was 10, I read Are You There, God? It’s Me Margaret, ” said Apatow, shouting out Blume. “It was funny, angsty, truthful and made me fall in love with reading. ” The actor and director then called out another female influence. “As a teenager, I got to watch a 20-something-year-old Lena Dunham write, direct, act and produce a truly groundbreaking show,” she said of Girls , produced by her father, Judd Apatow. She added, “But my favorite woman in film is my mom, Leslie Mann. ” Francesca Amiker, Tessa Thompson, Dede Gardner and Gabrielle Nadig, wearing Max Mara, speak onstage at the 2025 WIF Honors Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Janicza Bravo presented the the Crystal Award for Advocacy in Film award to Hedda ’s Tessa Thompson, Nia DaCosta (not present), Dede Gardner and Gabrielle Nadig. Lastly, Kaia Gerber honored her Palm Royale co-star Kristen Wiig with the inaugural Icon Award. “Who better to receive it than my favorite scene partner?” Gerber said. “For seven years at SNL , Kristen showed us comedy could be completely unhinged and utterly ‘stupid’ — a word I learned from Kristen herself as one of the highest forms of praise in comedy — and also, somehow be simultaneously deeply human. ” Kaia Gerber, Kirsten Schaffer, CEO, WIF and Icon Award recipient Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF Gerber continued, “When Bridesmaids came out, it was a revelation. … There is such truth and utter heartbreak behind [all of her characters]. ” She finished, “Tonight, we celebrate the woman who taught us that comedy is art, that chaos is beautiful, that sheer stupidity is not only encouraged but a necessity of life and that being unapologetically yourself might just be the most iconic move of all. ” An emotional Wiig thanked Gerber, who she called “a lighthouse” on her show. “I’m fully overwhelmed,” she said. “This is my first time having to make a speech like this. I just kept thinking, ‘How did I get here?’ … I keep coming back to the people who said ‘yes’ to me before I had anything on my resume. ” Wiig noted how her whole life changed when she joined The Groundlings. “That led to SNL ,” she said. She called out two men: Bridesmaids director Paul Feig and producer Judd Apatow (who reached out to her and asked if she wanted to write something). “I certainly wouldn’t be up here getting an award from Women In Film if it weren’t for that movie,” she said of the project that changed her life. Kristen Wiig Credit: Photo by Unique Nicole/Getty Images for WIF But ultimately, she’s enjoyed collaborating with women and exploring female characters. “I just love stories about women,” Wiig said. “We’re so crazy! We’re complex. We talk to each other about how we age, and our sensitivities and our intuition. It’s a never-ending source of material. I want to keep going,” she pledged. “I want to keep telling stories about women, with women. ” Wiig then offered everyone a challenge. “I still have things in my career that I really want to do — that I’m really scared to do,” she confessed. “And so I just thought, by chance, if everyone in this room has that thing that they’ve really wanted to do or really been scared to do — maybe we make like a collective pact with each other that we’re going to just do it, anyway. ” Don’t keep it to yourself…share the love! Certainly, the Epstein Files are current now,” executive producer and director Mimi Leder said ahead of Variety ‘s screening of the finale on November 19 in Los Angeles. “I’m not saying we’re doing that, I’m just saying it’s a constant theme, it seems, from the beginning of our show — from the Me Too movement to where we are today with the release of the files. On Tuesday evening, the publication hosted its annual rallying celebration of the changemakers who make us cry, laugh, and dream. With honorees, musical interludes, and even cheerleaders in attendance—it made for a crowd buzzing with big sleepover energy. Upon arrival to the grande dame hotel's Palm Court bar, guests gabbed over cocktails and chatted excitedly about the prospects of the historic mayoral election. (‘I Voted’ stickers peeked out proudly from clutch bags and evening coat lapels.) Once called to take their seats inside the rarely-seen Terrace Room, the program popped off energetically with riffs and raps from hip hop improv group Freestyle Love Supreme. This year's class of honorees were recognized for many reasons, with their bravery and courage to stand up and speak out being front and center. Demi Moore, elegant in Balenciaga and Jessica McCormack diamonds, was first up to the podium. “We need to keep building a world where women come together, not to compete out of scarcity, but to collaborate in abundance,” she said. “The truth is that when one of us shines, we all shine. And when one woman is seen, we are all seen. That is sisterhood.” Rachel Zegler, the 24-year-old actress spotlighted for being outspoken about her beliefs in the face of relentless tabloid takedowns, told the room: “I hope I get to be there when a young girl thinks she'll never be celebrated, so that I can tell her that she will. Because she always will. Women who stand for something will always, always be celebrated.” The evening encompassed all types of feelings and emotions, from Alex Newell's spine-tingling performance to the moment when Barry asked each person in the room to light up a bulb on their tables if any women in their life had been affected by breast cancer. (As one of the event's partners, Eli Lilly will extend the offer of free mammograms to women across the city). But it was educator and social media personality Ms. Rachel's acceptance speech that prompted floods of tears. Wearing a dress featuring artwork by children in Gaza that she advocates tirelessly for, she urged the room: “Every child everywhere has the right to be protected from violence and hunger, to have a home and medical care, and to go to school. As grown-ups, it's our moral responsibility to make sure that children's rights are respected and that we raise our voices when they're not.” The evening also honored South African chart-topper Tyla, glittering in Pandora jewelry, and the women of the WNBA including Jonquel Jones, Nyara Sabally, and Lexie Hull, whose call for “fair pay and safe play” had actress Karen Pittman clicking her fingers together in solidarity. Pat McGrath—the first makeup artist to ever become a Dame—was also given her flowers. “To every artist, every visionary, every young person with a dream; never dim your brilliance. The world needs your color, your creativity, your magic. Dream big, stay tall, and always make it major,” she said. As McGrath began her speech, the angle of the rhinestone-covered microphone was a little askew. Sitting in front of her, Demi Moore discreetly repositioned it to better amplify her words. Castro Published 7 days ago Amanda M. Castro is a Network TV writer at Collider and a journalist based in New York. Born and raised in Puerto Rico, Amanda is a bilingual Latina who graduated from the University of New Haven with a degree in Communication, Film, and Media Studies. She covers the world of network television, focusing on sharp, thoughtful analysis of the shows and characters that keep audiences tuning in week after week. At Collider, Amanda dives into the evolving landscape of network TV — from long-running procedural favorites to ambitious new dramas — exploring why these stories matter and how they connect with viewers on a cultural level. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap By turning Reese Witherspoon 's Bradley Jackson into a political prisoner in Belarus, The Morning Show doesn’t just end Season 4 with shock value — it resets every relationship she has, detonates UBN’s power structure, and reroutes the entire series heading into Season 5. The finale, “Knowing Violation,” brings together hostage diplomacy, corporate rot, family trauma, and a pair of last-minute confessions that permanently alter the show’s foundation. Bradley may make it home alive, but nothing about her world — or the show — looks the same. Bradley Jackson Can’t 'Reset' After This Reese Witherspoon as Bradley Jackson on The Morning Show Image via ©Apple TV+ / Courtesy Everett Collection Season 4 sends Bradley deeper into darkness than any storyline the series has taken on so far. When the finale opens, she’s been held for nearly a month inside a Belarusian detention site , tortured, sleep-deprived, and pressured to break her source. She refuses. She’s bruised, exhausted, but unbroken — a detail Charlotte Stoudt says was inspired directly by real-world hostage diplomacy cases like Evan Gershkovich and Brittney Griner. Stoudt notes that what struck the writers most was “the extremity of the conditions,” as well as the growing global trend of high-profile figures being detained and used as political leverage. That’s exactly what Bradley becomes: Leverage. Not a messy anchor navigating newsroom politics — a bargaining chip between a sanctioned oligarch, Celine Dumont's ( Marion Cotillard ) family empire, and the people back home who care enough to try to save her. But the critical shift is the cost of her rescue. Alex ( Jennifer Aniston ) puts her career — again — on the line, walking away from The Morning Show after Celine weaponizes Alex’s failed back-channel deal with Paul Marks ( Jon Hamm ). Chip ( Mark Duplass ) throws himself into the evidence Bradley had uncovered before she vanished. And Cory ( Billy Crudup ), whose heartbreak curdled into paralysis, is forced to confront both his grief and the truth his mother left behind: the original, unaltered Wolf River report, proof his own promotion came through a buried environmental cover-up. Bradley’s imprisonment becomes the collision point for all these unresolved fractures. When Alex finally reaches her on the tarmac in Minsk, the moment isn’t triumphant — it’s shell-shocked, raw. Bradley apologizes, believing she ruined everything. Alex tells her she didn’t ruin anything. She exposed it. Bradley isn’t coming back to the studio as the same person who left. You don’t survive a month in a Belarusian cell and return to “fiery morning anchor” banter. Season 5 has to reckon with a protagonist who’s endured trauma the show can’t handwave away, and who now sees the industry—and her closest relationships—with a clarity that’s going to be uncomfortable for everyone involved. Bradley’s Ordeal Blows 'The Morning Show' Up Alex holds a teary Bradley by the shoulders in The Morning Show. Image via Apple TV+ If Bradley’s cell is the emotional center of the finale, its fallout is the structural one. Her imprisonment is the fault line that splits UBN open. Every major power shift in the finale traces back to her. When Chip confronts him early in the episode, Cory refuses to help, too wounded by the end of his relationship with Bradley and too submerged in grief over his mother’s death. But the truth he’s been avoiding — that Martha Ellison helped bury the Wolf River findings and tied the family name to Celine’s father — becomes the thing he can’t run from. Stoudt describes it as the moment Cory realizes he’s “betraying [his] own values by not helping Bradley.” What follows is the first act of moral courage we’ve seen from him in seasons. Mia’s ( Karen Pittman ) investigation leads to a revelation that reframes the entire season: Celine orchestrated the deepfake of Alex to destabilize the network and consolidate power. When Alex confronts her, Celine flips the script, threatening to expose Alex’s Russian back-channel to the Marks family. It’s a devastating moment for Alex, who has sacrificed love, reputation, and health to stay in the room — only to be shoved out again. Stoudt describes Alex as “knocked sideways,” needing a beat before she could pick herself up and decide to fight back. Posts By Taylor Gates Sep 16, 2025 But the real undoing comes from Celine herself. When Alex holds her press conference, Celine panics, demanding Cory make it stop. In her rage, she reveals exactly how much influence her family had over Bradley’s detainment — unaware Cory has handed the phone to Alex, who broadcasts it live. Celine is finished instantly: exposed on air, summoned home, and almost certainly turned into her family’s scapegoat. Alex resigns mid-episode, but the press conference transforms that resignation into something else entirely: Power. She’s no longer the executive plaything shuffled out of boardrooms at the first sign of threat. She’s a public whistleblower with receipts. And as the dust settles, Mia and Ben ( William Jackson Harper ) trade a charged, wary face-off. Stoudt frames it as “a rivalry with a chemistry charge,” and the subtext is clear: there’s one vacant leadership seat, and two people ready to take it. By the time Bradley steps off the plane, UBN’s old hierarchy is gone . Its future — and its leadership — will be rewritten in Season 5. Alex and Cory Aren’t the Same People Anymore — and Their Season 5 Conflict Is Loaded Cory dipping Bradley while dancing in The Morning Show. Image via Apple TV The finale forces both Alex and Cory to confront patterns they’ve repeated for years. For Alex, the season peeling back her personal relationships — with her dad Martin ( Jeremy Irons ), with Paul, with Bro ( Boyd Holbrook ) — leaves her more emotionally exposed than ever. Her father’s unexpected return is what breaks the spell of paralysis. Stoudt says the message is simple: “You can talk about this. You are not alone.” It’s the validation Alex has been chasing her entire life, and it’s the spark that lets her reclaim control of the narrative. As for Cory, Season 4 becomes a crucible. He’s lost Bradley, lost his mother, and lost the illusion that he rose through UBN on merit alone. Miles’ ( Aaron Pierre ) accidental confession — that Celine brokered a deal with Martha ( Lindsay Duncan ) to bury the environmental findings in exchange for Cory’s promotion — devastates him. But it also gives him an out: The chance to choose what kind of person he wants to be after losing everything. He chooses Bradley. That choice, however heroic, puts him in direct conflict with Alex heading into next season. He saved Bradley, yes — but he also handed Alex the most explosive piece of audio the network has ever aired. Their partnership now rests on shared damage, shared betrayal, and a shared history of hurting each other when it matters most. Season 5 won’t be a return to the Alex/Cory power dance. It’s going to be a reckoning. Season 5 of 'The Morning Show' Is Teeing Up a Different Kind of War 'The Morning Show' Season 4 promotional image with Reese Witherspoon and Jennifer Aniston. Image via Apple TV+ By the final shot, the show has distilled itself back to its core players : Alex, Bradley, Chip, Mia, and Cory. But the surrounding terrain is unrecognizable. Alex is unemployed — and more dangerous than ever. Bradley is a survivor of political torture dragged back into the spotlight. Cory is morally reborn, but professionally exposed. Mia and Ben are circling the same chair, leaving UBN without a stable leader, a stable brand, or a stable public identity. Season 5 won’t be another cycle of corporate warfare inside a single network. It’s shaping up to be a season about who these characters become when the structures that defined them finally collapse. Bradley’s story was the spark. Everything else is the blaze that follows. Home Author Share Menu Free Speech CNSNews Culture Business Latino Latest Videos Testimonials Dark Mode Subscribe Donate About Us Contact Us Apple TV’s ‘Morning Show’ Claims Media Are ‘White Center-Right,’ Admits DEI ‘Doesn’t Work’ Dawn Slusher November 3rd, 2025 2:13 PM Text to Speech 00:00 00:00 Font Size It’s not much of a surprise when Apple TV’s liberal drama The Morning Show pushes leftist propaganda. But it is surprising when they basically admit how extremely far left they are by claiming the elitist media is a “corporate tool of the white center-right.” Such was the case in episode 6 of this season, “If Then,” which focused on Stella (Greta Lee), the CEO of the new UBN network who can’t stand white people, especially white men . Yet she’s still accused of not being “an ally” because she brought back disgraced former network president Cory (Billy Crudup), a move she was forced to make when Cory blackmailed her over her affair with the husband of UBN’s president and board member Celine (Marion Cotillard). The move negatively affected two women of color at the network: Mia (Karen Pittman), who quit and is now working as an agent for the other woman, Chris (Nicole Beharie). Just after Stella gives a noir -style soliloquy on legacy media being a “corporate tool of the white center-right,” Mia negotiates Chris’s contract with Stella. It’s at their meeting that Mia accuses Stella of “not being one of us” because she’s “surrounded by white people”: Stella: When Cory offered me Head of News, I laughed in his face. Legacy media, a corporate tool of the white center-right. I let him pay for lunch and I walked away. But he came back, like a migraine. He said I could push the stories I cared about. Drag the doubters, kicking and screaming, into the future. He told me to burn it down. Burn anyone who got in my way. Talent can't have editorial control over the news. It runs counter to our mission of objective reporting. You know that. Mia: [Cartoonish conservative talk-show host] Bro Hartman can say whatever he wants, whenever he wants. Stella: His show isn't news. I'm sorry, it's a nonstarter. And as for a producing pod, we don't have the money. And no one has cohost approval. Marcus: Alex Levy does. Stella: As Vice President of Talent, not as an anchor. Marcus: That's a distinction without a difference. Stella: Look. I understand that the response to her interview has been generally positive. Marcus: Yeah, that's an understatement. Stella: I get that you want a better deal. And I'm open to it. But not until the current deal is up. Mia: Deal is up now. Figure it out, or we're gonna go somewhere else. Stella: Would you give us a moment? Marcus: Take all the moments you need. Stella: So, what? Now you're trying to leverage me? Mia: I'm giving you a heads-up. That's more than you gave me. Stella: You're not getting this deal. I won't give it to you. And once Chris realizes that... Mia: Oh, she's realizing things. Like, you brought Cory Ellison back in the building. That's a hell of a move. And then giving him money and saying there's nothing left for us. Stella: He's making movies. It's different. Mia: You know, I remember when you got this job. You said you were gonna do it differently, do it right. And here you are, surrounded by white people and stepping on women of color to stay in that chair. You're not one of us. You never were. Later, as Stella enjoys another tryst with Celine’s husband Miles (Aaron Pierre), she excuses both her affair and her cutthroat business practices, claiming they came from her “inner straight white guy” who she “hates”: Stella: I took the job because it was impossible. I wanted the chance to fix something unfixable. Show the world that I could run the place without slitting any throats. That I could do it differently from Cory, from Paul. Then little by little, my inner straight white guy started clawing his way out... Telling me to get it done no matter what the cost. I hated that guy. So, I did what he would do. I fell into bed with the one person who could blow up my life. Trying to come to terms with her decisions, she has a conversation with the AI version of herself, which is part of an overall AI project Stella introduced to UBN to help advance the network into the future. Despite helping the company succeed financially, she bemoans the fact she hasn’t been able to push any DEI initiatives: Stella: Am I a good CEO? AI Stella: I think so. But, you know, I'm a little biased. Stella: What makes me good? AI Stella: You've cut costs. You've increased revenue. UBN stock is up 6% since you took over. Stella: So, money. AI Stella: Is there another metric? Stella: What about company culture? Opening doors for underrepresented groups. AI Stella: Like the Iranian fencer? Stella: No. Like our employees. AI Stella: The demographic shifts at UBN have been the same for the past five years. Stella: So, Mia's right. I am Cory 2.0. I'm not an ally. AI Stella: Do you think you're an ally? Stella: I made an Asian woman lick up a martini to close a deal. So, no. I guess not. I'm racist and sexist. And I stepped on people who look like me to get to where I am. AI Stella: If you didn't do that, would you have gotten the CEO job? Stella: Of course not. Because equality doesn't matter. Fairness doesn't matter. It doesn't make the stock move. Which is why it's only a matter of time before I get fired and replaced with a white guy, because at least he plays golf. AI Stella: You suck at golf. Stella: I f**king know that. But she made the stock move, so why would she be “fired and replaced with a white guy”? #MakeItMakeSense. It’s like the show accidentally made a case for imaginary oppression and false victimhood that’s so prominent on the left. When Stella gives a presentation on the AI project, AI Stella glitches and spills real Stella’s secret insecurities as well as her affair with Miles as Celine watches in shock: Man: A question. Host: Actually, I'm asking the questions but if it's a good one, go for it, dude. Stella: Yeah. Go ahead. Alex: No, no, no. Man: Is this a talent replacement tool or just a way to keep them in line? I ask because I heard Chris Hunter is being denied contract parity with white anchors at UBN. And that's why she's threatening to sit out the Olympics, and why she's boycotted today's event. Stella: Well, that's... Actually... AI Stella: Chris is great. We love Chris. But we all know DEI is dead. Also, it doesn't work. Maybe it never worked, and we were all just too afraid of the backlash to say it. Stella: It's okay, this is just an hallucination. I need to clarify that, of course, diversity is important to us at UBN. AI Stella: You mean we value diversity when we need the black anchor to save the day after an Iranian athlete defects on your watch. Man: What defection? And does the IOC know? Celeste: Stella. Turn it off. AI Stella: Then again, I'm racist and sexist . And I stepped over people who look like me to get to where I am. So, what do I know? Celeste: Stella. AI Stella: I'm racist and sexist. Celeste: Turn it off. AI Stella: Am I a bad person? Can a bad person be in love? I look at Miles, and I can't decide. Reporter: Are you talking about Celine's husband? AI Stella knows what’s up. DEI doesn’t work. And the irony in this scene is that Stella is most definitely racist and sexist, but not in the way the show wants us to believe. Her hatred has always been directed toward white men and women. The writers wanting us to think it’s the other way around is as ridiculous as them wanting us to believe their false claims about legacy media. Programming & Entertainment How Hello Sunshine's Flagship Event Made Every Attendee Feel Like the Main Character Last month, Reese Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine expanded Shine Away into a two-day festival featuring 2,000 guests, multi-stage programming, and immersive experiences designed to uplift women’s voices. Claire Hoffman , Senior Contributing Editor November 6, 2025 8 Min Read Reese Witherspoon's Hello Sunshine hosted its third annual Shine Away event at the Universal Studios Lot in mid-October. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media LOS ANGELES— Hello Sunshine’s Shine Away returned for its third year in mid-October, transforming LA's iconic Universal Studios Lot into a vibrant, two-day celebration of women’s stories, creativity, and connection. Produced by experiential agency Mirrored Media and connected by sponsor AT&T, the marquee consumer event welcomed up to 2,000 guests for a weekend centered around what Hello Sunshine calls “the joy of becoming.” “Our goal for Shine Away 2025 was to create an experience that reflects the full spectrum of what women deserve—more joy, more community, more connection, and more opportunity,” said Chris Bower , Hello Sunshine’s SVP of experiential and talent relations. “Building on the success of our first two years, we wanted this year’s event to feel expansive yet deeply personal: a place where women could recharge, reflect, and reignite their passions through authentic storytelling, immersive experiences, and meaningful connection.” Programming took place across three theaters and numerous breakout spaces—including a main stage set in a massive soundstage. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media "We expanded capacity to welcome up to 2,000 attendees and reimagined the footprint to feel more like a cultural festival," explained Bower. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media This year, Shine Away evolved into a true cultural festival, complete with interactive workshops, art installations, and a small business marketplace alongside its signature mainstage programming. The expanded footprint also extended the event’s reach to younger audiences, welcoming girls ages 13–17—aligning with the launch of Sunnie, Hello Sunshine’s new Gen Z–focused media, experiential, and lifestyle platform. “We responded to a powerful insight we’d heard from attendees over the past two years—that they wanted to share the Shine Away experience with their younger daughters and nieces,” Bower explained. “We introduced a dedicated Sunnie ticket for this audience and debuted a custom track of programming designed just for them, including an inspiring goal-setting workshop that encouraged Sunnie passholders to imagine—and begin shaping—their future path.” The event was produced by Los Angeles-based experiential agency Mirrored Media. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Balancing scale with intimacy was a key focus for Mirrored Media, which oversaw production across multiple stages and activations throughout the working studio lot—a challenge founder and CEO Justin Lefkovitch said the team approached through intentional design. “Shine Away is truly magical because of the guest experience,” he said. “We made a conscious effort to expand the event so more people could share in that magic, but it was essential that we didn’t lose the intimacy and personal connection Shine Away is known for.” He added, “Every stage, seating area, and breakout space was crafted to encourage connection, engagement, and meaningful conversation. Even the main stage, which filled a massive soundstage, was designed to feel warm and inviting, like a portal to incredible storytelling and shared inspiration.” Shine Away was created in response to the insight that women, facing unprecedented levels of burnout, are unable to find time to focus on themselves. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media The weekend opened with stand-up comedy from Yvonne Orji, followed by a welcome from Hello Sunshine founder Reese Witherspoon and AT&T’s chief marketing and growth officer Kellyn Smith Kenny, who joined Mariska Hargitay and Karen Pittman for a conversation about connecting passion with purpose. Across three theaters and numerous breakout spaces, sessions unfolded with a mix of star power and vulnerability—from Monica Lewinsky’s fireside chat on letting go of perfection to Lilly Singh and Malin Åckerman’s discussion on the power of female friendship. Day two was equally star-studded, featuring speakers like Ellie Kemper, Angela Kinsey, Molly Sims, Ali Wentworth, and Justina Blakeney. “Our programming philosophy starts with the belief that every woman has a story worth sharing," said Bower. "We curate our lineup across industries—entertainment, entrepreneurship, wellness, finance, and beyond—to reflect the modern woman’s multifaceted identity." Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media "This year, we were intentional about pairing high-profile cultural voices with emerging changemakers, ensuring each session delivered both inspiration and tangible takeaways," he added. "We also extended our storytelling beyond the stage, featuring many of our speakers across Hello Sunshine’s editorial and social channels in the lead-up to the event." Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Behind the scenes, the scale of the production required meticulous coordination. “We had dedicated teams assigned to each zone; every theater, breakout space, and activation had its own producers, stage managers, and operations crew,” Lefkovitch explained. “Three theaters ran simultaneous programming throughout the day, each functioning independently with its own show callers, stage managers, and talent runners. All of these teams ultimately rolled up to a master show caller and central talent team, who monitored timing across the entire site.” Producing within an active studio lot also presented challenges. “Unlike a traditional event venue, we were working within soundstages and operational studio spaces,” Lefkovitch said. “That required close collaboration with Universal’s security, facilities, and production teams to ensure we created a seamless experience for guests while maintaining safety and minimizing disruption for Universal employees.” "Because it’s an active production environment, there were additional layers of logistics and compliance—building and safety and fire considerations that aren’t typical in standard event venues. But those extra steps were always in the best interest of guest safety and the integrity of the lot itself," said Lefkovitch. “The Universal Studios Lot team were truly incredible partners." Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Immersive brand activations served as both engagement and empowerment zones. Presenting sponsor AT&T’s Connection Plaza, a new addition this year, gave guests a space to fuel both their personal and professional journey. Attendees engaged in mentorship sessions and interactive workshops, and also took new headshots in the AT&T Headshot Studio. Another AT&T-branded space invited guests to record messages for their future selves. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Guests also shopped female-founded small businesses and enjoyed various experiences from Drop of Sunshine, Happy Coffee, Owl’s Brew, smartwater, Sol de Janeiro, The Goods Mart, Zibby’s Bookshop, and more. "We also leaned into even deeper sponsor integration [this year], ensuring brand activations and programming offered enhanced value to our guests—whether through mentorship, creative expression, or professional development," said Bower. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media In another space, Wells Fargo helped foster confidence through financial programming, while Novartis’ “Your Attention Please” campaign brought breast cancer awareness to life in a cheeky yet powerful way. Guests followed an interactive path through an educational maze that culminated in a red-carpet moment, where a robotic glam bot filmed attendees striking confident poses. “The camera zoomed in and ended on the guest’s chest, creating a playful yet powerful piece of shareable content that drove home the importance of breast health,” said Lefkovitch. “It was smart, cheeky, and memorable—exactly the kind of storytelling that turns awareness into connection.” Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Hello Sunshine also showcased its owned brands through the Reese’s Book Club Book Lovers Experience, which sold out within 48 hours. Bower noted that from the moment doors opened, the energy was high as fans connected over their shared love of reading and met some of their favorite authors. “It was a beautiful reminder that storytelling doesn’t just live on the page—it lives in the connections we create around it,” he said. "The energy in the Reese’s Book Club Bookshop is always unmatched," said Bower. "The passion of our readers is truly at the heart of what makes Reese’s Book Club so special." Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media "From the moment doors opened, you could feel the joy and anticipation as fans connected over their shared love of reading, met some of their favorite authors, and bonded with one another in meaningful, genuine ways," he added. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media For the Hello Sunshine team, Shine Away is more than an event—it’s a manifestation of their mission to put women at the center of every story. “Hello Sunshine was founded on the belief that when women’s stories are told, the world becomes a brighter place,” said Bower. “Shine Away brings that mission to life in the real world. It’s where our storytelling turns into community. Through Shine Away, we create space for women to connect over shared experiences, discover new perspectives, and feel seen and celebrated.” "Ultimately, our goal was for every guest to feel seen, welcomed, and part of something special, no matter where they were on campus," agreed Lefkovitch. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media The success of this year’s event is already shaping what’s next for the company’s experiential strategy, from next week's inaugural Sunniefest for Gen Z women in Dallas to a planned New York edition of Shine Away, along with Reese’s Book Club experiences set for 2026. “Shine Away’s success has shown that women are seeking more than inspiration—they’re craving connection, community, and actionable growth,” Bower said. “Each new [event] format is designed to meet our growing audiences where they are, offering fresh ways to learn, connect, and evolve. Together, these experiences form an ecosystem that supports women and girls at every stage of their journey.” VENDORS Production: Mirrored Media Audio and Projection: ShowPro Lighting Design: Lightswitch Fabrication: IDF Studio Scenery Graphics: AFI Venue, F&B, Rigging: Universal Studios Lot Rentals: Found Rental Co. , FormDecor , Designer8 , Town & Country Event Rentals About the Author Claire Hoffman Senior Contributing Editor Claire Hoffman is an award-winning writer, editor, and content strategist. Sunshine's Flagship Event Made Every Attendee Feel Like the Main Character Last month, Reese Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine expanded Shine Away into a two-day festival featuring 2,000 guests, multi-stage programming, and immersive experiences designed to uplift women’s voices. Claire Hoffman , Senior Contributing Editor November 6, 2025 8 Min Read Reese Witherspoon's Hello Sunshine hosted its third annual Shine Away event at the Universal Studios Lot in mid-October. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media LOS ANGELES— Hello Sunshine’s Shine Away returned for its third year in mid-October, transforming LA's iconic Universal Studios Lot into a vibrant, two-day celebration of women’s stories, creativity, and connection. Produced by experiential agency Mirrored Media and connected by sponsor AT&T, the marquee consumer event welcomed up to 2,000 guests for a weekend centered around what Hello Sunshine calls “the joy of becoming. ” “Our goal for Shine Away 2025 was to create an experience that reflects the full spectrum of what women deserve—more joy, more community, more connection, and more opportunity,” said Chris Bower , Hello Sunshine’s SVP of experiential and talent relations. “Building on the success of our first two years, we wanted this year’s event to feel expansive yet deeply personal: a place where women could recharge, reflect, and reignite their passions through authentic storytelling, immersive experiences, and meaningful connection. ” Programming took place across three theaters and numerous breakout spaces—including a main stage set in a massive soundstage. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media "We expanded capacity to welcome up to 2,000 attendees and reimagined the footprint to feel more like a cultural festival," explained Bower. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media This year, Shine Away evolved into a true cultural festival, complete with interactive workshops, art installations, and a small business marketplace alongside its signature mainstage programming. The expanded footprint also extended the event’s reach to younger audiences, welcoming girls ages 13–17—aligning with the launch of Sunnie, Hello Sunshine’s new Gen Z–focused media, experiential, and lifestyle platform. “We responded to a powerful insight we’d heard from attendees over the past two years—that they wanted to share the Shine Away experience with their younger daughters and nieces,” Bower explained. “We introduced a dedicated Sunnie ticket for this audience and debuted a custom track of programming designed just for them, including an inspiring goal-setting workshop that encouraged Sunnie passholders to imagine—and begin shaping—their future path. ” The event was produced by Los Angeles-based experiential agency Mirrored Media. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Balancing scale with intimacy was a key focus for Mirrored Media, which oversaw production across multiple stages and activations throughout the working studio lot—a challenge founder and CEO Justin Lefkovitch said the team approached through intentional design. “Shine Away is truly magical because of the guest experience,” he said. “We made a conscious effort to expand the event so more people could share in that magic, but it was essential that we didn’t lose the intimacy and personal connection Shine Away is known for. ” He added, “Every stage, seating area, and breakout space was crafted to encourage connection, engagement, and meaningful conversation. Even the main stage, which filled a massive soundstage, was designed to feel warm and inviting, like a portal to incredible storytelling and shared inspiration. ” Shine Away was created in response to the insight that women, facing unprecedented levels of burnout, are unable to find time to focus on themselves. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media The weekend opened with stand-up comedy from Yvonne Orji, followed by a welcome from Hello Sunshine founder Reese Witherspoon and AT&T’s chief marketing and growth officer Kellyn Smith Kenny, who joined Mariska Hargitay and Karen Pittman for a conversation about connecting passion with purpose. Across three theaters and numerous breakout spaces, sessions unfolded with a mix of star power and vulnerability—from Monica Lewinsky’s fireside chat on letting go of perfection to Lilly Singh and Malin Åckerman’s discussion on the power of female friendship. Day two was equally star-studded, featuring speakers like Ellie Kemper, Angela Kinsey, Molly Sims, Ali Wentworth, and Justina Blakeney. “Our programming philosophy starts with the belief that every woman has a story worth sharing," said Bower. "We curate our lineup across industries—entertainment, entrepreneurship, wellness, finance, and beyond—to reflect the modern woman’s multifaceted identity. " Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media "This year, we were intentional about pairing high-profile cultural voices with emerging changemakers, ensuring each session delivered both inspiration and tangible takeaways," he added. "We also extended our storytelling beyond the stage, featuring many of our speakers across Hello Sunshine’s editorial and social channels in the lead-up to the event. " Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Behind the scenes, the scale of the production required meticulous coordination. “We had dedicated teams assigned to each zone; every theater, breakout space, and activation had its own producers, stage managers, and operations crew,” Lefkovitch explained. “Three theaters ran simultaneous programming throughout the day, each functioning independently with its own show callers, stage managers, and talent runners. All of these teams ultimately rolled up to a master show caller and central talent team, who monitored timing across the entire site. ” Producing within an active studio lot also presented challenges. “Unlike a traditional event venue, we were working within soundstages and operational studio spaces,” Lefkovitch said. “That required close collaboration with Universal’s security, facilities, and production teams to ensure we created a seamless experience for guests while maintaining safety and minimizing disruption for Universal employees. ” "Because it’s an active production environment, there were additional layers of logistics and compliance—building and safety and fire considerations that aren’t typical in standard event venues. But those extra steps were always in the best interest of guest safety and the integrity of the lot itself," said Lefkovitch. “The Universal Studios Lot team were truly incredible partners. " Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Immersive brand activations served as both engagement and empowerment zones. Presenting sponsor AT&T’s Connection Plaza, a new addition this year, gave guests a space to fuel both their personal and professional journey. Attendees engaged in mentorship sessions and interactive workshops, and also took new headshots in the AT&T Headshot Studio. Another AT&T-branded space invited guests to record messages for their future selves. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Guests also shopped female-founded small businesses and enjoyed various experiences from Drop of Sunshine, Happy Coffee, Owl’s Brew, smartwater, Sol de Janeiro, The Goods Mart, Zibby’s Bookshop, and more. "We also leaned into even deeper sponsor integration [this year], ensuring brand activations and programming offered enhanced value to our guests—whether through mentorship, creative expression, or professional development," said Bower. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media In another space, Wells Fargo helped foster confidence through financial programming, while Novartis’ “Your Attention Please” campaign brought breast cancer awareness to life in a cheeky yet powerful way. Guests followed an interactive path through an educational maze that culminated in a red-carpet moment, where a robotic glam bot filmed attendees striking confident poses. “The camera zoomed in and ended on the guest’s chest, creating a playful yet powerful piece of shareable content that drove home the importance of breast health,” said Lefkovitch. “It was smart, cheeky, and memorable—exactly the kind of storytelling that turns awareness into connection. ” Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media Hello Sunshine also showcased its owned brands through the Reese’s Book Club Book Lovers Experience, which sold out within 48 hours. Bower noted that from the moment doors opened, the energy was high as fans connected over their shared love of reading and met some of their favorite authors. “It was a beautiful reminder that storytelling doesn’t just live on the page—it lives in the connections we create around it,” he said. "The energy in the Reese’s Book Club Bookshop is always unmatched," said Bower. "The passion of our readers is truly at the heart of what makes Reese’s Book Club so special. " Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media "From the moment doors opened, you could feel the joy and anticipation as fans connected over their shared love of reading, met some of their favorite authors, and bonded with one another in meaningful, genuine ways," he added. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media For the Hello Sunshine team, Shine Away is more than an event—it’s a manifestation of their mission to put women at the center of every story. “Hello Sunshine was founded on the belief that when women’s stories are told, the world becomes a brighter place,” said Bower. “Shine Away brings that mission to life in the real world. It’s where our storytelling turns into community. Through Shine Away, we create space for women to connect over shared experiences, discover new perspectives, and feel seen and celebrated. ” "Ultimately, our goal was for every guest to feel seen, welcomed, and part of something special, no matter where they were on campus," agreed Lefkovitch. Photo: Courtesy of Mirrored Media The success of this year’s event is already shaping what’s next for the company’s experiential strategy, from next week's inaugural Sunniefest for Gen Z women in Dallas to a planned New York edition of Shine Away, along with Reese’s Book Club experiences set for 2026. “Shine Away’s success has shown that women are seeking more than inspiration—they’re craving connection, community, and actionable growth,” Bower said. “Each new [event] format is designed to meet our growing audiences where they are, offering fresh ways to learn, connect, and evolve. Together, these experiences form an ecosystem that supports women and girls at every stage of their journey. ” VENDORS Production: Mirrored Media Audio and Projection: ShowPro Lighting Design: Lightswitch Fabrication: IDF Studio Scenery Graphics: AFI Venue, F&B, Rigging: Universal Studios Lot Rentals: Found Rental Co. , FormDecor , Designer8 , Town & Country Event Rentals About the Author Claire Hoffman Senior Contributing Editor Claire Hoffman is an award-winning writer, editor, and content strategist.
