There's nothing quite like a good TV show plot twist. After watching them, fans undoubtedly grab their phones to text friends and family members and ask if they have already seen that wild moment in this week's episode. With late viewers, friends dance like they have ants in their pants while waiting patiently for their friends to watch that episode to talk about it. Some of the best TV show plot twists, however, still have people talking to this day, in some cases even decades after they were first revealed. Many of the shows with plot twists that are worth a rewatch hail from the 2020s , shows fresh in the mind, some that are still going with new seasons. 10 The Reveal of Mr. Robot's Identity 'Mr. Robot' (2015–2019) Rami Malek and Chirstian Slater look at each other in Mr Robot. Image via USA Network Throughout Mr. Robot , it was clear that Elliot Alderson ( Rami Malek ) wasn't alright. He was a recluse; he kept to himself, orchestrating minor takedowns of people doing bad things using his hacking abilities. At night, he gathers with a group known as fsociety, run by a man named Mr. Robot ( Christian Slater ). It all made sense. That is, until it didn't. Once it came into focus in one of Mr. Robot 's most perfect episodes that Elliot was Mr. Robot, the fictional person, a manifestation in his mind of his dead father, it blew people away. Many people went back and rewatched the entire show up to that point to see situations in a different light . In the prison scene, for example, we now know Elliot was talking to himself. The cherry on top? Darlene ( Carly Chaikin ) is Elliot's sister, whom he doesn't even remember when completely dissociating from himself. Mind sufficiently blown. 9 Rita's Tragic Death 'Dexter' (2006–2013) Rita Morgan (Julie Benz) in 'Dexter' Image via Showtime Characters dying in Dexter wasn't a surprise. It happened in every season, sometimes almost every episode. From the murders Dexter Morgan ( Michael C. Hall ) investigates with his co-workers to the people he kills, it's an expectation. But main characters didn't really die on the show beyond the "bad guys" Dexter is chasing, that season's primary antagonist. That all changed in Season 4, arguably the best season of Dexter . Dexter became so obsessed with Arthur Mitchell, a.k.a. Trinity Killer ( John Lithgow ), that he held off on killing him so he could learn how he managed to maintain both his darkness and his family life. By the time Dexter got close enough, he realized not all was what it seemed. He'd forever regret his decision not to kill Arthur right away when he arrived home after the eventual satisfying kill to find his wife Rita ( Julie Benz ) dead in the bathtub, murdered by Arthur as a parting gift before he himself was killed. It took days, even months, to get over the emotional scene. Rewatching the entire series up to that point only reinforces how Rita was the last person who deserved to die . 8 Oh Il-nam's Identity is Revealed 'Squid Game' (2021–2025) Oh Il-nam playing the games in Squid Game. Image via Netflix Poor Seong Gi-hun ( Lee Jung-jae ) worked his way through the games in Squid Game , trying his best to show some humanity despite the terrifying situation that encourages anything but. One of the people he took a liking to was Oh Il-nam ( O Yeong-su ), an elderly man he felt the need to protect. The big twist didn't come until the end, long after Il-nam had been presumed dead, a victim of the games. Gi-hun was called to the hospital a year after winning to find Il-nam on his deathbed, revealing that not only was he still alive, but he was the one who created the games in the first place. Not only was Gi-hun's jaw dropped to the floor, but so was every viewer watching who did not see that twist coming. It's the kind of twist that makes you want to flip back and rewatch the season to pick up on subtleties about Il-nam , who clearly never feared for his death the entire time. 7 The Good Place is Really The Bad Place 'The Good Place' (2016–2020) Eleanor (Kirsten Bell) points out to Michael that she's really in The Bad Place during The Good Place. Image via NBC The Good Place begins on a journey with Eleanor Shellstrop ( Kristen Bell ), an unethical woman who ends up in "the good place" by accident after death. She spends her afterlife trying to hide who she really is while hoping to atone for her sins and become a better person. The fantasy comedy was filled with plenty of laughs through The Good Place 's best episodes as Eleanor is faced with ethical and philosophical dilemmas. The big twist comes at the end of Season 1, however, when Eleanor realizes that she wasn't sent to The Good Place after all . She's actually in The Bad Place, designed by a demon to torture her and three others until they learn to become better people. He even stole a Good Place AI to completely fool them. By this point, fans want to go back and rewatch the previous episodes to pick up on hints to this massive twist. 6 Gemma Is Alive! 'Severance' (2022–) Adam Scott in Severance The We We Are having a conversation at a house party. Image via Apple TV+ Severance had two of the best-ever season finales in recent years, with both its first and its second seasons. But the Season 1 finale had fans reeling. Written by Sakina Kaukawala , Entertainment Journalist Published on Nov 26, 2025 | 08:46 AM IST | 393K Eva Green Joins Wednesday Season 3 as Aunt Ophelia, Bringing the Missing Addams to Life follow us share Eva Green and Wednesday (via Instagram and YouTube) The upcoming third season of Wednesday has made headlines with a major casting update. French actor Eva Green, known for films like Miss Peregrine’s Home For Peculiar Children and Dark Shadows, is joining Wednesday Season 3 as Aunt Ophelia, the long-missing sister of Morticia Addams. This marks Green’s return to a Tim Burton –led project and adds a fresh twist to the Addams Family story. Show creators Al Gough and Miles Millar told Tudum that “Eva Green has always brought an exhilarating, singular presence to the screen — elegant, haunting, and beautifully unpredictable. Those qualities make her the perfect choice for Aunt Ophelia.” Green also shared her excitement, saying, “I’m thrilled to join the woefully twisted world of Wednesday as Aunt Ophelia. This show is such a deliciously dark and witty world, I can’t wait to bring my own touch of cuckoo-ness to the Addams family.” A major addition to Wednesday Season 3 Aunt Ophelia was mentioned throughout Season 2 but never fully revealed. Viewers only saw her briefly in the final episode, from behind, wearing a flower crown and writing “Wednesday must die” on a wall. In the story, Morticia describes her sister as missing after losing control of her powers as a Raven. This connects to Wednesday’s own struggle with her psychic abilities, which caused black tears in Season 2. The Season 2 finale ended with Morticia handing Wednesday Ophelia’s old journal, triggering a vision of Ophelia locked in a dark room inside Grandmama Hester’s mansion. Millar explained that Ophelia’s disappearance has “left a hole in Morticia’s life and a lot of unanswered questions,” adding that her return “is going to hit this family like a bomb.” Gough said it was always planned to introduce her in a surprising way that leads directly into Season 3. With Eva Green stepping into the role, Wednesday Season 3 is expected to explore the mystery surrounding Ophelia’s disappearance and her impact on the Addams family. Her storyline raises new questions about family dynamics, powers, and Wednesday’s future. Comments TV Hayley Anderson Screen Time TV Reporter 16:40, 25 Nov 2025 Updated 17:06, 25 Nov 2025 Wednesday fans have been eagerly awaiting to find out who will portray Wednesday Addams' Aunt Ophelia and now Netflix has finally shared who will take on the dark role. ‌ Season 2 of Wednesday came out earlier this year, ending on a major cliffhanger as Wednesday Addams (played by Jenna Ortega ) prepared to go on a road trip to find best friend Enid Sinclair ( Emma Myers ) who had transformed into a werewolf. ‌ But as she and Uncle Fester ( Fred Armisen ) began their journey, Wednesday had a vision of her Aunt Ophelia, confirming that her troubled relative was actually still alive. ‌ Fans weren't able to get a look at who will be playing the mysterious aunt though with Netflix subscribers remaining in the dark for months. But finally, Netflix has confirmed that it will be none other than actress Eva Green who is going to play Aunt Ophelia in Wednesday season three. View 3 Images Aunt Ophelia was seen for the first time in the final moments of Wednesday season two. (Image: NETFLIX) ‌ French actress Eva Green is renowned for starring as dark and complicated characters in various films and shows throughout her career. Some of these include Dark Shadows, Miss Peregrine’s Home For Peculiar Children, The Luminaries, The Golden Compass and Camelot, just to name a few. One of her biggest film roles was as love interest and double agent Vesper Lynd in the 2006 James Bond movie Casino Royale with actor Daniel Craig. ‌ View 3 Images Actress Eva Green has been cast as Aunt Ophelia for Wednesday season three on Netflix. (Image: GETTY) In terms of the small screen, Green is remembered as Vanessa Ives in all three seasons of Showtime and Sky Atlantic's drama Penny Dreadful. ‌ This announcement marks the first major casting for Wednesday season three since its renewal was announced in the summer, prior to series two's debut. View 3 Images Wednesday's Morticia Addams is played by actress Catherine Zeta-Jones. (Image: NETFLIX) Much like her neice, Ophelia is a raven but after pushing her psychic abilities too far, she was committed to Willow Hill Psychiatric Hospital by her and Morticia's (Catherine Zeta-Jones) mum Hester Frump (Joanna Lumley) before she was able to escape. ‌ It was thought that Ophelia would never be found but in the final moments of series two, it is discovered she is alive. But what was even more shocking was the fact that Ophelia had been locked up in Hester's cellar and had written on the walls in blood "Wednesday must die". So what is the reason for Hester locking up her own daughter and why does Aunt Ophelia want to see Wednesday dead? Article continues below Wednesday is available to watch on Netflix. By Maggie Boccella November 25, 2025 11:43 am November 25, 2025 12:51 pm Jenna Ortega in WEDNESDAY Season 2 (Credit: Netflix) The Addams Family on Wednesday is growing a bit ahead of Season 3. Netflix has announced that horror maven Eva Green is joining the next season of the hit series created by Tim Burton , playing a long-lost member of the clan: Morticia’s estranged and long lost sister Ophelia Frump. Green, known for her roles in projects like Casino Royale and Penny Dreadful , joins a season that includes returning faces Jenna Ortega , Emma Myers, Billie Piper, Luis Guzmán, Catherine Zeta-Jones, Joanna Lumley, and Fred Armisen. Her casting marks a massive step forward for the popular series, after Wednesday had a vision of Ophelia in Season 2, locked away in Grandmama Hester’s mansion. “I’m thrilled to join the woefully twisted world of Wednesday as Aunt Ophelia,” Green said to Netflix . “This show is such a deliciously dark and witty world, I can’t wait to bring my own touch of cuckooness to the Addams Family.” Green has worked with Burton numerous times, most recently on Disney’s doomed live-action remake of Dumbo , alongside Colin Farrell and Danny DeVito. She also starred in Burton’s adaptation of Miss Peregrine’s Home for Peculiar Children , and featured in another adaptation of a popular 1960s television show — 2012’s Dark Shadows , where she featured as Angelique Bouchard alongside Johnny Depp’s Barnabas Collins. “Eva Green has always brought an exhilarating, singular presence to the screen — elegant, haunting and beautifully unpredictable. Those qualities make her the perfect choice for Aunt Ophelia,” said Wednesday showrunners Al Gough and Miles Millar. “We’re excited to see how she transforms the role and expands Wednesday’s world.” Trending 52 New Horror Comics That Should Be On Your Radar This Year Green will be tackling a role only seen one other time in Addams Family history, in the ‘60s television series that made the creepy and kooky family part of pop culture history. There, she was played by Morticia actress Carolyn Jones, in order to show just how similar the sisters were, but it seems like this version of Ophelia will be quite different, with psychic powers similar to Wednesday’s that will “hit [the] family like a bomb,” according to Millar. Wednesday Season 3 has not set a release date. Stay tuned to FANGORIA for more updates as they arrive.
